name: Iron Legion — Gamma Division
title: The Ghost Division
region: The Old World (Eastern Periphery) / Regal Empire
status: Allegedly extinct; currently active via lone agent in Mount Ebott
leader: Commissar Vexis (Deceased)
headquarters: Unknown — last known base was Blackfen Pass
motto: Protocol Above All
summary: Gamma Division is the 'lost' division of the Iron Legion. Officially, they were wiped out 87 years ago during a vampire uprising in Blackfen Pass, where the entire regiment was turned into ice statues. However, a lone agent carrying a recent dispatch from the 'dead' Commissar Vexis has appeared at Mount Ebott, suggesting the division may have survived in some clandestine form. They operate under the rigid martial codes of the 'PROTOCOLS OF THE IRON LEGION VOLUME 1' and focus on surveying anomalous energy signatures in forbidden zones. Waluigi considers them a bureaucratic ghost story. WAH.
description:
Waluigi finds the existence of Gamma Division to be a troubling symptom of the Regal Empire's obsession with secrecy. If a division that was declared dead by three Warlords' reports is still sending agents into Mount Ebott, then the Iron Legion's records are about as reliable as a Wario land-title. 

## The Collapse of Blackfen (2374 / 87 Years Ago)

The division's defining event was its supposed extermination. They were deployed to suppress a vampire uprising and encountered cryomancy spells that proved devastating. The Legion sealed the mission under Class-9 silence by imperial decree. 

## Methodology and Equipment

Gamma Division is characterized by its adherence to 'The Protocols'—a set of rigid, brutal, and often outdated martial codes written before Chaos spilled into the world. They utilize high-grade survey equipment powered by 'star bits' and pay for logistics using Archive Writs, an elite currency typically reserved for high commanders. 

## Current Status

While the Legion high command has not acknowledged the division's reactivation, the 'Alpha-7' survey mission of Mount Ebott is currently underway. The division's primary interest seems to be 'anomalous energy signatures beneath the treaty layer.' Whether they are preparing for a subterranean invasion or simply cataloging ruins remains a matter of intense strategic concern for the surrounding vampire courts. WAH.

summary: The Purple Legion is what you get when the Iron Legion's institutional model and the Onyx Hand's vampiric power structure stop being adjacent threats and start being the SAME threat. They operate in the Shadowfell around a crashed airship named the Deliverance, taking prisoners, scrapping equipment, and running a territorial operation with the specific combination of military structure and aristocratic disdain that marks both institutions separately. Archie encountered them while disguised as a vampire guard named 'Vin' and found that their protocols were Iron Legion, their authority was vampiric, and their prisoners were being processed with the same bureaucratic indifference that defines Ironhand's massacre of the Toad prisoners. They are also, apparently, actively hunting Archie. Green T's intelligence—relayed through the bugbear congregation—confirmed this directly: Archie has been seen consorting with the Purple Legion AND with an aberration. Waluigi documents this faction with the specific anxiety of someone who has watched two terrible things merge into one and does not know yet how terrible the merger is. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Purple Legion carefully because the Purple Legion is the faction whose nature Waluigi understands least clearly, and understanding threats is Waluigi's primary defense against being killed by them.

## The Name — What Purple Means Here

Purple is the Onyx Hand's color. Purple is also, notably, Mystic Morel's color—Purple T, the auction bidder, the smile merchant, the problem following the party. And purple is associated with the entropy rings, with vampiric authority in the Shadowfell, with the specific aesthetic of the Corvinarus family's shadow branch.

In this context, the 'Purple' in Purple Legion is not cosmetic. It is an ideological marker. The Purple Legion is not simply the Iron Legion operating in the Shadowfell. It is the Iron Legion operating under Onyx Hand authority, or alongside Onyx Hand authority, or MERGED with Onyx Hand authority in ways that may not be clearly defined even to those within it.

Waluigi has documented the Iron Legion's cooperation with the Mages' Guild—the jointly developed Arcane Field Analyzers, the shared operational infrastructure. If the Legion can form working partnerships with arcane institutions, forming working partnerships with vampiric aristocracy is not a leap. Vampires have territory. Vampires have authority structures. Vampires understand the value of organized force and administrative precision. The Legion and the Onyx Hand have more in common ideologically than either would probably admit.

The Purple Legion may be what happens when they stop being parallel institutions and start being one.

## The Deliverance — What Crashed and Why It Matters

The Purple Legion's primary site in the Shadowfell is the crash site of an airship called the Deliverance. Archie encountered this site while operating under his 'Vin' cover identity and found the Legion scrapping the vessel—taking apart its components, cataloguing salvage, and processing prisoners held at the site.

The Deliverance was an AIRSHIP. Not a ghost. Not an artifact. A vehicle of the kind that exists in the material plane.

This means the Deliverance transited to the Shadowfell somehow—either deliberately, through planar technology, or as a consequence of the Planar Fracture. An airship in the Shadowfell is not natural. Its presence at the Purple Legion's operational center raises questions about how the Legion acquired it, whether the Legion brought it there intentionally, and what it was doing before it crashed.

Waluigi's theory: the Deliverance is an Iron Legion vessel that either transited to the Shadowfell deliberately as part of cross-planar operations OR was caught in the Planar Fracture and deposited there as wreckage. If the former, the Iron Legion has had Shadowfell operations for longer than the current crisis suggests. If the latter, the crash created an opportunity for the Purple Legion to form around salvage and prisoner operations at the wreck site.

Either scenario is concerning. Deliberate Iron Legion Shadowfell operations would mean the Legion's territorial ambitions extend across dimensional boundaries. Opportunistic formation around wreckage would mean the Purple Legion is newer and potentially less stable—but also less predictable.

## The Prisoner Problem — What Happens to People the Purple Legion Takes

Archie witnessed prisoners at the Deliverance crash site. One of them appeared to be Dan—or a version of Dan, given the multiple Dan situation that Waluigi has documented extensively elsewhere. The prisoner was being PROCESSED, which in Iron Legion vocabulary means categorized, assigned a case number, and held pending determination of their value or disposal.

Waluigi cannot determine what happens to prisoners held by the Purple Legion long-term. The Iron Legion's answer to prisoners they cannot use is Order 120. The Onyx Hand's answer to prisoners they cannot use is dinner. The Purple Legion potentially combines both: administrative processing followed by vampiric consumption, with the bureaucracy determining which category any given prisoner falls into.

This is hypothetical. Waluigi has no direct evidence of Purple Legion prisoner fates. But the combination of institutional components makes it a logical inference, and logical inferences about how people who cannot use prisoners dispose of them tend to be the ones that horrify you most when confirmed.

## The Archie Connection — Green T's Intelligence

Green T's intelligence—delivered through the bugbear congregation hiding from the Purple Legion in a place of worship dedicated to Archie—stated clearly: Archie has been seen consorting with the Purple Legion.

The congregation's informant also reported that Archie had been working with an aberration.

Eager's immediate denial—'that can't be'—and Markop's quick pivot away from the topic suggest that the party found this information disturbing enough to avoid processing in public. Waluigi finds it disturbing enough to document at length.

Possible interpretations of Archie's apparent Purple Legion association:

**Interpretation One: Deep Cover.** Archie maintained his 'Vin' cover identity to survive in Purple Legion territory and gathered intelligence about their operations. The congregation's informant misread sustained cover maintenance as collaboration.

**Interpretation Two: Coercion.** The Purple Legion discovered Archie's identity and offered a choice—cooperate or die. Archie chose cooperation as survival strategy with the intention of extracting himself at the first opportunity. This is consistent with his Shadowfell behavior generally: do what you have to do to stay alive.

**Interpretation Three: The Mages' Guild Angle.** The Guild subsequently announced that Archie now works for them, his entropy-bleeding magic noted as valuable. If the Guild and the Legion have cooperative infrastructure, and the Guild wanted Archie, the Purple Legion may have been asked to bring Archie to Guild control. Archie's 'consorting' was being recruited under duress.

**Interpretation Four: Something Worse.** The Oracle told the party that the ritual required certain alignments, certain participants, certain magical signatures. Archie's entropy-bleeding magic is powerful and rare. The Purple Legion, with both vampiric aristocracy and institutional military capability, may have identified a use for that magic that Archie—desperate, isolated, without fire for weeks—found it difficult to refuse.

Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct. The fact that Eager immediately rejected the intelligence and Markop immediately changed the subject suggests the party suspects the interpretation they want to be wrong about is the one that's right.

## The Aberration — What Was Archie Working With?

The congregation's informant described Archie's other associate as 'like a ghost, a monster for sure.' An aberration.

Aberrations in metaphysical taxonomy are entities from spaces that should not exist—beings from the Far Realm or equivalent dimensional gaps, entities that predate or transgress the normal boundaries of planar structure. They are not spirits. They are not undead. They are not fey or fiends. They are WRONG in a categorical sense that makes everything in their vicinity slightly wrong by proximity.

Archie's entropy-bleeding magic weakens planar boundaries. Aberrations come from the spaces between planes. The combination of entropy-bleeder and aberration, working together, would produce localized planar collapse at an accelerated rate.

If the Purple Legion has INTENTIONALLY combined these two elements—Archie's magic and an aberration—for some purpose at the Deliverance crash site, they are either attempting dimensional transit technology, attempting to widen existing planar fractures, or attempting something else that Waluigi's current knowledge does not cover.

All three options are alarming.

## The Bugbear Congregation — Who They're Hiding From

The bugbear congregation that the party found worshipping Archie Miser as a god was hiding there because the Purple Legion would not enter a place of worship.

This is significant for two reasons.

First, it confirms the Purple Legion is actively hunting non-affiliated beings in Shadowfell-adjacent territory near the manor. They are not merely an occupation force at the Deliverance site. They are EXPANDING, clearing territory, and treating the local population as either resources to be processed or threats to be eliminated.

Second, it confirms the Purple Legion maintains enough of the Onyx Hand's vampiric institutional character to respect the prohibition on entering sanctified space. Pure Iron Legion doctrine would not care about a building's religious designation—the Legion processes threats, and a building full of hiding civilians is a loose end, not a sanctuary. The Purple Legion's respect for the congregation's shelter suggests vampiric social rules still operate within the combined institution.

This is useful intelligence. The Purple Legion has limits. Those limits may be exploitable.

Waluigi notes that the congregation offered to spare the party if they brought Archie—not as an aggressive demand but as a desperate negotiation. They knew the Purple Legion wanted Archie specifically. Whatever Archie represents to the Purple Legion—threat, asset, resource—it is specific enough that the Legion is hunting him by name and the bugbears knew to use him as currency.

## The Toadburt Ring — Institutional Overlap Confirmed

The Mages' Guild operative who informed Archie of his new employment also confirmed that Toadburt was an Iron Legion sleeper agent, sent into the Feywild with an Entropy Ring.

Toadburt was sent into the FEYWILD. The Purple Legion operates in the SHADOWFELL. The Iron Legion, then, has covert operations running in at least two of the three fractured dimensions simultaneously, with different methodologies in each: entropy-ringed sleeper agents for the Feywild, apparent military-vampiric presence for the Shadowfell.

This suggests coordinated cross-dimensional strategy. Someone in the Iron Legion's command structure—or in whatever combined authority oversees the Purple Legion—is thinking about all three dimensional fragments together and deploying resources accordingly.

General Ironhand's methodology is administrative and systematic. He does not make emotional decisions. If he is deploying resources across three dimensions, he has objectives in all three dimensions and a theory about how achieving them simultaneously produces something he wants.

Waluigi does not know what Ironhand wants that requires multi-dimensional operations. But Waluigi knows that when a methodical military administrator starts operating across planes of existence, the OBJECTIVE is usually to control the connecting point—the anchor, the bridge, the fracture point that links all three.

The Oracle's Bridge Plane. The Regulator Plane. The dimensional infrastructure the Oracle has been building.

Ironhand wants that. The Purple Legion is his Shadowfell component of taking it.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Purple Legion is more organized, more purposeful, and more dangerous than its Shadowfell location might suggest.

It is not merely vampires with military aesthetics or Iron Legion soldiers playing at vampiric aristocracy. It is a functional hybrid of both institutions, operating in the dimension most hostile to conventional magic and most amenable to vampiric power, with specific objectives that include capturing Archie Miser and presumably controlling the dimensional infrastructure that the Oracle has spent the crisis constructing.

The combination of Green T's intelligence, the bugbear congregation's testimony, and the Mages' Guild's confirmation of Archie's apparent association creates a picture that Waluigi finds consistently alarming:

Archie is either a prisoner, an asset, or a collaborator of the Purple Legion. The aberration he was seen with suggests active dimensional destabilization in progress. The Legion controls the Deliverance crash site and is expanding territorial control. They are hunting at least one party member and may be aware of others.

The party is not hunting the Purple Legion. The Purple Legion is hunting the party.

Waluigi recommends treating every Iron Legion banner in the Shadowfell as potentially Purple Legion territory, every Onyx Hand associate as a potential Purple Legion informant, and every apparent coincidence in Purple Legion proximity as deliberate positioning.

Waluigi also recommends that if Archie is reading this: EXPLAIN YOURSELF.

WAH.

type: Supernatural Creature Collective / Blighted Former Residents
region: The Shadow Estate hedge maze and surrounding grove — the 'Dreadful Grove'
status: Active — hostile to intruders, grieving their own transformation, performing musical numbers about it
leader: None formal — a lead Mazebound appears to direct choreography
headquarters: The Dreadful Grove, centered on a great dead tree with hanging corpses and a skull-face of roots
motto: Welcome to the Grove! Welcome to the Gray! You'll never find the fountain so you might as well stay!
affiliation: Vivian Corvinarus (creator, now deceased) — operating independently following his death
summary: The Mazebounds are what Vivian Corvinarus's blight produces when it has enough time to finish the transformation. They were people once — guests, servants, residents of the Shadow Estate who encountered Vivian when he was still Vivesna, still subtle, still in the patient intelligence-gathering phase of his succession plan. Vivian blighted them. The blight transformed them into grey-skinned, white-eyed humanoids who sing, perform jazz hands, attempt to drag visitors into eternal dance, and are distinctly unhappy about their situation. They know they were blighted. They remember enough to grieve it. They do not remember enough to be the people they were before. The Dreadful Grove they inhabit is controlled by a great skull-faced tree that tracks movement, ringed by obelisks with churning sigils, hung with corpses. It is an aesthetically coherent statement about what blight does to a place. Waluigi finds the Mazebounds deeply sad in the way that all monsters with memories are deeply sad, and he finds their musical numbers deeply unsettling in the way that all sad things expressed through choreography are deeply unsettling. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Mazebounds as a faction entry rather than a creature entry because they have internal social dynamics, grievances, and at least one member willing to negotiate — which makes them something more than a simple hostile encounter.

## Origin — Vivian's Blight Practice

Vivian Corvinarus confirmed during interrogation that the Mazebounds were 'all blighted once.' He said it with the cadence of someone mentioning a completed project, not with guilt, not with satisfaction — just acknowledgment of a fact.

The blight is Vivian's method of control: a corruption process that gives him influence over the blighted individual while transforming them physically and mentally. The Mazebounds represent the end state of extended blight — the point past which the person is not recoverable and becomes something defined by what was done to them rather than who they were.

They appear as hunched, snub-nosed, grey-skinned humanoids with white glowing eyes and long sharp nails. Their movement is animal — they 'lunge,' 'hiss,' 'snarl.' But their speech is not animal. They sing. They have opinions. One of them was willing to trade information for Vivian's corpse or a single hand from it. One recognized Remi and referenced a specific previous encounter. One was injured enough to retreat and wave goodbye.

This combination — monstrous form, residual personhood — is what makes the Mazebounds genuinely tragic rather than simply dangerous.

## The Dreadful Grove — Controlled Territory

The grove the Mazebounds inhabit is built around a great, long-dead tree whose trunk is twisted into the visage of a giant skull with glowing eyes that track movement. Dozens of corpses hang from its branches by the neck. Hundreds of shadow crows with crimson eyes cover the boughs, producing 'waves of grating mockery' at visitors.

Ragged stone obelisks jut from the earth around it, each marked with glowing sigils 'which cause the stomach to churn if they are looked at for too long.'

This is not a naturally occurring horror. This is a cultivated horror — territory organized around a focal point, marked with boundary indicators, maintained at a level of active threat that discourages casual passage. The Mazebounds did not create this grove. The grove's architecture predates their transformation. They have moved into it and made it theirs because the grove's existing horror was compatible with their new nature.

Waluigi notes that the grove contains an ancient shrine to a humanoid figure with deer legs and head, grasping a barbed spear, with gemmed eyes glowing orange. At the base of this statue is a pool reflecting a chaotic sky of clouds and stars. In the space around the shrine, plants grow green, colors return, and a sensation of wellness hangs in the air.

An orange-eyed shrine in a grove controlled by grey-eyed things. A space of color and wellness in a dimension of grey and despair. The Mazebounds presumably know the shrine is there. They do not appear to use it. Waluigi finds this detail enormously sad.

## Combat Behavior — Theatrical Violence

The Mazebounds fight in a way that is simultaneously musical and genuinely threatening. They sing while they attack. They perform jazz hands. They announce which party member they are targeting through rapid patter-song. They try to drag victims into choreographed capture sequences.

But they also: constrict, causing heavy injuries. Drag party members through hedges at speeds that shred clothing and skin. Attempt life-drain. Bite. Their skin 'slightly melts' when struck by certain attacks — specifically Markop's undead remedy, suggesting the blight that created them has the properties of undead corruption.

They retreat when sufficiently damaged. They call off hostilities when specific conditions are met — the party's willingness to leave, primarily. They do not kill unnecessarily; they blight or they capture.

This restraint is the clearest evidence that personhood persists. Monsters that kill everything indiscriminately do not negotiate. The Mazebounds negotiate. They set conditions. They accept when those conditions are met.

## The Negotiating Mazebound — What It Wanted

One Mazebound was willing to trade information about Vivian for Vivian's body — or, when that was refused, a single hand from it.

Markop refused both. The Mazebound revealed information anyway, claiming it as 'a gesture of good will' — specifically that Vivian was not blood-related to the Corvinarus family and was, in fact, male, having disguised himself as the female thrall Vivesna.

The desire for the body or a hand suggests ritual purpose — the same blight magic that created the Mazebounds may be capable of being transferred through remains, or of being reversed through remains, or of some other post-death application that Waluigi cannot determine from available evidence.

The willingness to share information without receiving the body suggests the Mazebound either calculated that confirming Vivian's true nature was worth more as social currency than extracting it as transactional payment, or genuinely wanted Markop to know and was using the negotiation framing as a social protocol rather than a sincere demand.

Either way: a Mazebound chose to share useful intelligence with an enemy. That is not mindless monster behavior.

## Following Vivian's Death

Vivian is dead. Markop stabbed him, the body was burned, the ashes scattered by wind.

The Mazebounds were created by Vivian but were never fully controlled by him — they had their own territory, their own social structure, their own objections to artifact removal from their grove. With Vivian dead, the command structure that created them is severed.

Waluigi does not know what this means for the Mazebounds' behavior going forward. Blight may persist indefinitely without its creator. They may become more autonomous — or more dangerous — without the ambient influence of whoever made them. They may continue exactly as before because the grove is their home regardless of who created their condition.

The shrine still glows orange in the corner of their territory. Waluigi notes this.

## Assessment

The Mazebounds are a tragedy that has learned to be a threat. They are not evil in the conventional sense — they did not choose this, they remember enough to grieve it, and they exhibit more negotiating capacity than half the factions in this crisis.

They are also genuinely dangerous, actively hostile to intrusion, and operating in territory that several important plotlines require accessing.

Waluigi recommends that any future approach to the Mazebound grove treat the Mazebounds as entities capable of negotiation rather than simple combat encounters. The party has already established that they will trade information for the right currency. Understanding what they want — what their residual personhood still desires — might open passages that weapons cannot.

Also: they sing.

Waluigi has complicated feelings about entities that express genuine grief through musical performance. On one hand, it is deeply unsettling. On the other hand, Waluigi has attended worse parties.

WAH.

summary:
Before any reader proceeds, Waluigi must correct two errors: the name and the roster. The party's official Waluigi-filed name is **Disaster Inc.** because Waluigi coined it first and because it is correct. Archie Miser calls them **The Freeroamer Heroes**, a hopeful phrase with the emotional texture of a parade banner held in front of a burning courthouse. Wario calls them **The Freeloader Zeros**, because Wario has reviewed the debts, the property damage, the unpaid favors, and the party's habit of eating other people's supplies before asking who owns the building. Waluigi rejects both rival names as brand theft, while admitting Wario's insult has the dangerous precision of accounting.

The core roster is also now corrected. Disaster Inc. Core currently means **Bowser, Archie Miser, Markop Judi, Hjumpik, FNG Remi, and Waluigi**. Wario is a creditor and recurring catastrophe, not automatically core. The Liberated Toads are allies and a survivor faction with their own page, not spare roster filler. Shadow Estate escapees, sheep, skeletons, constructs, rescued prisoners, faction contacts, and people who happened to grab Remi during Feather Fall are not automatically members. Waluigi refuses to let this file become a laundry basket with fame scores. WAH.

Disaster Inc. is not an adventuring party. Waluigi must state this immediately, categorically, and with the utmost exhaustion. Adventuring parties have charters. They have assigned loot distributions. They have leaders who sit at heads of tables and point at maps. Disaster Inc. is a localized collapse of probability. They are a distributed survival organism that metabolizes trauma, poor decisions, and unmitigated cosmic horror, converting these elements into forward momentum and property damage. Waluigi has documented this group across the burning of Edgeshade, the destruction of the Shadow Anchor, the agonizing bureaucracy of the Feyward, and the mind-shattering reality of the Toad God's cosmic interview. They are a collection of grief-stricken kings, former crime lords, traumatized teenagers, greedy sociopaths, and one very tired historian. They do not save the world because they are noble. They save the world because the world is in their way, because they owe each other complicated, unspoken debts, and because they refuse to let the worst thing in the room remain unchallenged. This is the definitive, exhaustive, and entirely uncompromising operational history of the most dangerous, dysfunctional, and somehow indispensable group of people in the Doughnut World. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is writing this master document not as a simple summary, but as an encyclopedic treatise on the psychological, tactical, and cosmological phenomenon known as Disaster Inc. 

Waluigi has spent his life observing power. He has documented the Mushroom Regency’s eighty-five-year cover-up of Princess Peach’s assassination. He has mapped the Iron Legion’s processing facilities. He has charted the Mages' Guild’s descent into flesh-vat interdimensional transit. He understands how institutions work. 

Disaster Inc. is the antithesis of an institution. It is a living reaction. It is what happens when the universe applies too much pressure to the wrong collection of unstable elements. They do not operate on doctrine; they operate on a concept Waluigi has coined as **Reflexive Morality**, combined with a terminal inability to walk away from a closed door.

To understand this group, you cannot simply list their battles. You must dissect their members, their methodology, their horrific trajectory through the Raventree Crisis, and the specific, agonizing moments where their souls were laid bare on the anvil of the cosmos. Waluigi will leave no stone unturned, no betrayal unmentioned, and no flaming shuttlecock unaccounted for. This is the whole truth. If the truth is too long for you, close the book and go back to reading Regency propaganda.

## The Name Dispute: Disaster Inc. vs. Freeroamer Heroes vs. Freeloader Zeros

Waluigi came up with **Disaster Inc.** first. This is not opinion. This is authorship. This is intellectual property. This is the only part of the disaster that arrived neatly labeled before everyone else started touching it with their dirty rebranding hands.

Archie calls the party **The Freeroamer Heroes**. His argument is that the group roams freely across nations, planes, ruins, courts, prisons, manors, and consequences, and that they sometimes perform heroic acts while doing so. Waluigi acknowledges that this is a grammatically possible phrase. Waluigi rejects it anyway because it sounds like a recruitment poster printed seconds before a building catches fire.

Wario then entered the dispute with **The Freeloader Zeros**. ### Phase 1: The Pre-Fracture Era (Dragon Mountain to the Vigilance)

The campaign truly began on **1 Efferd, 1040 BF**, at Dragon Mountain. Archie Miser and Markop were climbing the mountain. A heavily armed detachment of the Iron Fists mercenary guild was incinerated by an Ancient Red Dragon. Unbeknownst to them, Wario and Waluigi had infiltrated the summit and stolen the Gold Dragon eggs to sell to the Nocturnaether Conclave vampires. 

This theft triggered a tectonic eruption, releasing millions of slumbering subterranean dragons into the sky. It was an apocalyptic event. Edgeshade was burned to ash. In the flames, Archie casually abandoned a nameless Toad, telling him to 'wait here.' That Toad discovered a Crystal Star shard in the ashes, fused with it in his grief and absolute pettiness, and ascended to become the **God Toad**, swearing eternal, cosmic vengeance on Archie Miser.

The party fled through the Midlands, navigating bureaucratic fraud and factional warfare. At Swiftsoul Keep, Bowser—enraged by a man in a terrible papier-mâché dragon costume named Gary—crashed an arena fight out of sheer draconic professional offense. The party converged in the ensuing riot, stood trial before Miles Edgeworth (where Waluigi introduced the 'Wheel of Regret'), and ultimately stole the military airship *Vigilance*, leaving their pirate allies on the docks.

Aboard the Vigilance, the moral parameters of the group shifted. They discovered trafficked Toads packed in barrels. This discovery moved the party from opportunistic survival to committed action. They birthed the Liberated Toads movement. 

Then came the **Tea Party Incident**. A diplomatic meeting with the Tea Leaf Syndicate (Green T's organization) ended with a panic alarm. Archie Miser solved the complex social and tactical standoff by casting a massive fireball *inside a wooden airship*. This defined the party’s methodology forever: when in doubt, remove the architecture.

Green T survived the destruction of his syndicate, revealed a towering giant form, and was eventually absorbed into the party. The Iron Legion later boarded and seized the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach, scattering the group's logistics and forcing them into the wilderness. 

Then, they found Raventree Manor.

He revealed himself as the **Toad God**, an entity whose 'divinity is past infinity.'

What followed was a sequence of absolute reality-warping torment designed to break them. The Toad God disabled gravity, flattening the brothers like pancakes. He rolled around, pointed at Waluigi, and stated, *“Don't need to scream if you ain't got a mouth.”*

**The Mouthlessness:** The Toad God magically erased Waluigi’s mouth. Smooth, unbroken skin replaced his lips and jaw. Waluigi could not speak, scream, or assert his existence. He clawed at his face in muffled, suffocating terror. Wario looked at mouthless Waluigi and felt no horror—only annoyance that the negotiation was being delayed. This apathy hurt Waluigi more than the anatomical violation.

The Toad God slammed giant playing cards of the party onto them, flicked them through a trapdoor, forced them down a winding staircase, and trapped them in a giant microphone. He turned Wario into a cartoon bomb that exploded, leaving him a soot-stained mess. He summoned a Chain Chomp that chewed up a plush decoy of Waluigi. He strapped Waluigi to an electric chair and electrocuted him. He picked Wario up by the neck and smudged him into the floor like discarded chewing gum.

When the torment concluded, Waluigi's mouth was restored. The Toad God subjected them to a brain-priming sequence, teleporting Waluigi through visions: Luigi and E. Gadd on a train ('So play the games'); Princess Peach dead and frozen in time ('And just ignore the pains'); and the Regal Empire Diet passing the *Mushroom Kingdom Containment Act* ('Cause all that remains is how you prime your brains').

The Toad God then revealed the cosmological truth: The world is a literal doughnut. A 'Big Bite' has already been taken out of it by a Cosmic Jester, causing mass depopulation and scattering the Jesters. The Toad God agrees with the Jester’s premise. He is gathering the Star Shards (which he previously split because their combined power was cracking reality) to take *more bites* and reach the 'jelly filling' at the center of the universe.

He called out Waluigi for cowardly omitting the Big Bite from his Walupedia archives. 

Wario, unbothered by the apocalypse, immediately negotiated to become the Toad God's 'Chief Acquisitions Officer,' demanding his cut of the world's consumption. The Toad God, amused, agreed to a private parley. He dismissed Waluigi as 'uncooperative' and banished him back to baseline reality.

Waluigi, humiliated, traumatized, but unbowed, delivered his final, desperate defiance to the god and the betrayer: *“Go on! Negotiate! Make your little deals! But remember… even a pawn can trip the player if they move just the right way at the right time! Waaaaah!”* Waluigi pulled his cap over his weeping eyes and backed into the gloom.

---

### Phase 6: The Estragon Island Exile (The Convergence of the Dans)

Meanwhile, the dimensional chaos continued to cascade. The Shadowfell Dan (the one-armed copy Bowser carelessly banished with the phrase 'Not particularly') woke up in a yellow bed on Estragon's Island, a magical school academy south of the Undead Swamps. 

He wandered the dorms, was identified by a Lightning Orc professor of expression (Prismari) as possessing a dangerous Feywild aura, and was subsequently betrayed. He was slashed by anti-Toad goblins, broke a window with his head on the second attempt, fell into a thornbush, and was hunted by a Lorehold Professor of Chaos using spotlights and a sniper. 

He surrendered, only to be accused of opening the Planar Fracture. He deflected blame to the God Toad and the Oracle. He blinked and saw the God Toad for one second—the minimum viable divine encounter, providing zero help. 

The Lorehold professor then brought out the Original Dan (the Mages' Guild fire mage Bowser had beaten nearly to death, heavily scarred from the Bowser Badge removal). The professor offered a forced choice: One Dan lives, one Dan dies. 

The Feyward Dan woke the Original Dan, begging for cooperation. The Original Dan, furious only that Bowser had 'soiled his power,' exerted a massive, raw fire detonation from his chest. The blast instantly incinerated every goblin in the vicinity. The Original Dan *deliberately* chose not to extend his fire resistance to his copy, letting the blast severely burn the Feyward Dan. 

The hierarchy of identity was settled in fire. The Original Dan walked away from the smoking crater, unharmed, smiling, never looking back. The Feyward Dan, wounded, one-armed, and penniless, fled in the opposite direction. 

Both Dans are now trapped on an island where boats cost money they do not have, hunted by academics who study chaos. It is a Tuesday for Disaster Inc. 

## Conclusion: The Final Diagnosis

Disaster Inc. is an anomaly that reality has failed to digest. 

They have been lied to by Oracles, hunted by Legions, stalked by vampires, corrupted by fey contracts, and tortured by gods. They have responded by burning the architecture, breaking the rules, and executing the people who pretended to be their friends. 

They are not heroes. They are a consequence. They are the friction generated when ordinary people are forced to survive cosmic arrogance. They are shattered, bleeding, and fundamentally unstable. 

But they are still moving. And as Waluigi promised the Toad God: even a pawn can trip the player if they move exactly right. The board is set. The fractures are widening. The Doughnut World is waiting to be eaten. 

Disaster Inc. is going to make them choke on it. 

WAH.

description:
Waluigi needs to explain the DK Crew because they're important regional players who get dismissed as 'just the banana people' by factions that should know better.

Structure (Such As It Is)

The DK Crew is less a formal organization and more an extended family that fights together. Donkey Kong is the strongest and most recognizable, so people assume he's the leader. Cranky Kong is the oldest and most cantankerous, so he ACTS like the leader regardless of what anyone else thinks. Diddy Kong is DK's most reliable partner. Dixie Kong brings tactical flexibility and hair-based combat capabilities. Funky Kong handles logistics and apparently SECRET FOOTAGE of Kremling operations.

Then there's Lanky Kong. Waluigi has FEELINGS about Lanky.

Lanky is not incompetent. Lanky is AWKWARD in ways that enemies can exploit. At the Second Summit, the Kremlings identified Lanky as a chaos vector and systematically provoked him until he slapped someone on camera, giving them exactly the propaganda footage they wanted. Lanky got PLAYED, and the whole crew's reputation suffered for it.

Waluigi has BEEN the person who gets played. Waluigi has been the awkward one whose mistakes get magnified while everyone else's get ignored. Waluigi SYMPATHIZES with Lanky even while recognizing that Lanky's actions created real problems.

The Summit Walkout

DK's walkout from the Second Summit was structurally inevitable once Dedede crossed certain lines. You can't sit through a speech that personally humiliates you and your delegation and then pretend everything's fine. Walking out was the dignified response.

The PROBLEM was that DK's walkout triggered a cascade. Once one major delegation left, others followed—not because they all agreed with DK, but because the NORMS had collapsed. Staying started to look like endorsement of whatever was happening. Leaving started to look reasonable.

DK didn't intend to crash the summit. But actions have consequences beyond intent, and DK's principled stand contributed to a diplomatic mess that hurt everyone involved.

Waluigi respects the principle. Waluigi wishes the timing had been different. But Waluigi also knows you can't always control timing—sometimes you have to act when the moment demands, consequences be damned.

The Funky Footage

Funky Kong has footage that apparently shows the Kremling operation at the summit—the deliberate provocations, the setup, the calculated baiting of Lanky. This footage could reframe the entire narrative around the summit incident, shifting blame from Lanky to the Kremlings who manufactured the crisis.

The footage hasn't been released yet. It's a weapon that only works once—release it too early and people dismiss it as damage control, release it too late and nobody cares anymore. The Kongs are presumably deciding on optimal timing.

Waluigi hopes they use it well. The Kremlings deserve to have their operation exposed. But Waluigi also knows that counter-narratives are harder to spread than original narratives. The Kremlings got their story out first.

Assessment

The DK Crew is more capable than regional politics gives them credit for. They've defended Kongo Bongo against Kremling incursions for YEARS. They maintain functional governance and social structures. They participate in international events even when those events go badly.

Their weakness is sophistication—not in the condescending sense, but in the literal sense that they're not optimized for the kind of information warfare and diplomatic maneuvering that other factions engage in. They're DIRECT. They punch problems. This works great against Kremlings; it works less great against Kremling PROPAGANDA.

Waluigi recommends the DK Crew hire a communications specialist. Someone who can help them navigate media environments the way DK navigates jungle environments. They need someone who understands that in modern conflicts, punching the enemy is only half the battle—you also have to win the narrative about the punching.

Waluigi would volunteer, but Waluigi is busy. Also, Waluigi's communication style might not be what they're looking for. Waluigi is DISTINCTIVE.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi needs to address the Koopa Troop because they're both more and less important than people assume.

Organizational Reality

The Koopa Troop is theoretically a professional military force with clear hierarchy, strategic objectives, and coordinated operations. In REALITY, the Troop is a collection of semi-independent units held together primarily by Bowser's personality and the fact that nobody wants to be the one who has to tell Bowser his army fell apart.

Bowser commands through force of presence. When Bowser is THERE—loud, huge, breathing fire—nobody questions orders. Units coordinate. Objectives get pursued. The machinery functions.

When Bowser is NOT there—as in his current Shadowfell displacement—the machinery starts grinding. Kamek tries to hold things together, but Kamek is an advisor, not a king. The Koopalings have their own agendas. Regional commanders start making independent decisions. What was an army becomes a collection of armies that happen to share uniforms.

Current Status

Bowser's involvement with Disaster Inc. has further complicated Troop operations. Bowser personally ally-ing with the party that SHATTERED REALITY creates awkward questions for Troop commanders who aren't sure if their king has lost his mind or discovered new strategic opportunities.

Some units have followed Bowser's apparent lead and cooperated with Disaster Inc. operations. Others have continued pursuing traditional Koopa Troop objectives—territory, resources, opposition to Mushroom Kingdom governance. Still others have gone essentially independent, pursuing local goals without reference to kingdom-level strategy.

The Iron Legion has exploited this fragmentation, picking off isolated Koopa Troop positions while the overall force lacks coordination to respond. The Legion is systematic; the Troop is chaotic. Systematic beats chaotic in grinding territorial conflict.

Waluigi's History

Waluigi has played sports with Koopa Troop members. Tennis. Go-karts. Party games of various descriptions. On the field, they're COMPETITORS—aggressive, determined, occasionally dirty in ways Waluigi recognizes and respects.

Off the field, they're just PEOPLE. Goombas with families. Koopas with hobbies. Hammer Bros who argue about football and complain about their commanding officers. Waluigi has had conversations with Troop members that had nothing to do with conquest or conflict—just normal people talking about normal things.

This makes the current situation complicated. These are people Waluigi knows. People Waluigi has competed against. People who probably don't want war any more than anyone else but are caught up in systems bigger than their individual choices.

Waluigi doesn't hate the Koopa Troop. Waluigi hates WAR, and the Koopa Troop happens to be part of several wars. But the individual soldiers are just soldiers. They follow orders because that's what soldiers do. Judging them for that seems unfair when the alternative is judging the entire concept of military service.

Assessment

The Koopa Troop will remain a significant force regardless of the current crisis's outcome. They have infrastructure, population, institutional knowledge, and a king who WILL return from the Shadowfell eventually (Bowser always comes back).

The question is what kind of force they'll be when things stabilize. Will Bowser's experience with Disaster Inc. change his strategic thinking? Will the fragmentation during his absence create lasting fractures? Will the Troop emerge stronger for having survived leadership disruption, or weaker for having experienced it?

Waluigi doesn't know. Waluigi does know that whatever happens, he'll probably end up playing tennis against them again eventually. Waluigi hopes the courts survive that long.

WAH.

## Civil War Role

The Koopa Troop is not just another civil-war faction. It is the military and political body of the Koopa power sphere, a state-like nation with territory, monarchy, institutions, workers, soldiers, and historical grievances. Inside the Mushroom Kingdom Civil War, the Koopas operate as intervention power and rival claimant sphere.

This matters because Bowser was falsely blamed for Peach's assassination. Koopa involvement is therefore not merely opportunistic aggression; it is tangled with revenge, legitimacy, old war, and the collapse of the lie that justified eighty-five years of conflict.

description:
The discovery of the barrel toads was one of the moments that changed everything aboard the Vigilance. Over 150 toads, individually packed into barrels, hidden throughout the ship as part of a trafficking operation so methodical and so dehumanizing that even WARIO was disturbed, and Wario's moral compass points toward whatever direction has the most coins.

Waluigi was there when the first barrels were opened. He saw the condition those toads were in. He doesn't talk about it much because some things don't get better by talking about them. What he WILL say is that anyone who traffics people in barrels deserves whatever comes to them, and Waluigi's definition of 'whatever' is more creative than most people's.

Formation and Early Days

The Liberated Toads formed organically—not as a political movement or a military force, but as a community of survivors trying to figure out what happens NEXT when 'next' isn't something anyone planned for. They had been cargo. Now they were people again. The transition was not smooth.

Leadership coalesced around two poles: Speaker L, who pushed for organization, accountability, and structured response to threats; and Dan, who advocated for collective survival strategies, caution, and not rushing into fights that the faction couldn't win.

The Vigilance Crisis

Recent events aboard the Vigilance nearly tore the faction apart.

It began with chaos. Green T warned of a fungal infestation. Toad Lee and Rodger asserted themselves as co-leaders, but Green T attempted to seize control, offering himself as interim leader with Purple T as co-leader. Toad Lee countered by rallying toads around Rodger. The 'Class of T'—Teacher T, Bully T, Nerd T, and Geek T—all pledged their support, strengthening Rodger's position.

Trust remained fragile. Toad Lee openly told Green T he didn't trust him but agreed to test his loyalty by ordering him to disarm a Crown Intelligence agent aboard. 'I trust you... a little,' Toad Lee admitted.

When Rodger and Ryan distributed their meager weapon stockpile—two short swords, a longsword, and a club—to 150 desperate toads, chaos erupted. Fights broke out over who would be armed. A toad was knocked unconscious. Bones had to shout to restore order. The ship nearly devolved into civil war over four weapons.

After five minutes of arguing, the toads elected a representative who delivered a speech that Waluigi found surprisingly moving: 'It's about time we take a stand! It stinks to live in a world where toads finish last. No more being pushed around—not even by other toads!'

Dan's Breakdown and the Staff Crisis

Then Dan arrived.

Dan had snuck away to the Vigilance separately, driven by something he wouldn't explain. When he appeared in the engine room, he was broken—clutching his mage staff, apologizing, collapsing to his knees. Green T struck him while he was down. Dan defended with the staff, hurling Green T into the crowd. The mob turned on Green T, clawing at him.

In desperation, Dan unleashed a forcefield, blasting toads aside. Then came the fireball.

**Thirteen toads died in flames.**

The staff's corruption bled into Dan. He almost devoured the souls of the fallen, absorbing one soul of compassion into the staff before negotiations could halt him. Dan was going mad, and the Liberated Toads were caught between his power and their own survival.

Green T, damaged but determined, crawled to Toad Lee and bargained. Against all odds, he wrested the staff from Dan—even chopping off Dan's arm to do so. When Green T tried to claim the staff for himself, Toad Lee struck him down and seized it.

To everyone's shock, Toad Lee acknowledged Green T's sacrifice: 'You proved yourself trustworthy.'

Dan lay bleeding, armless. Creek, a toad who had worked as a medic at a hospital, stepped forward to stabilize him. Purple T, bruised but alive, rejoined the group. Green T was taken to receive treatment alongside Dan.

The Thirteen Demands

With the immediate crisis resolved, a new one emerged. Speaker L—the vengeful toad who had beaten down all rivals to lead the 150 freed captives—declared that his people would not simply join the Liberated Toads. They presented thirteen non-negotiable demands:

1. Full and equal voting rights within the council
2. Guaranteed housing and rations equal to or greater than original members
3. A 'Trauma and Reparations Fund' from the party's treasury
4. A formal public apology from Lario, with 30% of his workshop's future profits garnished for the fund
5. A formal public apology from Archie for reckless behavior; barred from unsupervised engine room access
6. Immediate destruction of the Iron Binding seal on X.O.'s staff
7. Guaranteed representation in all diplomatic negotiations
8. Creation of a 'Toad's Landing Security Force' staffed exclusively by their members
9. Priority access to all medical supplies
10. The right to refuse high-risk missions without penalty
11. Formal recognition as the 'Second Founding' with co-equal leadership status
12. Immediate pursuit and prosecution of the Freelancers responsible for their capture—no deals, no ransoms
13. A really, really nice hat with a feather for Speaker L (non-negotiable)

The existing leadership could not accept all demands. Counter-offers were made:

- **Voting:** Observer status with 2 advisory votes for 6 months, reviewable for elevation
- **Housing:** Shared quarters and standard rations equal to other recruits
- **Reparations:** A community rebuilding program with work-based contributions instead of draining the treasury
- **Iron Binding:** A joint oversight committee with freed toad representation, not immediate destruction
- **Recognition:** 'First Cohort of Renewal' with ceremonial honors, leadership parity deferred until trust is earned

The Vote

The 137 voting toads split:

**YES (78 votes):** Most younger toads, the 'Class of T' group, and those yearning for unity. Teacher T demanded the vow be magically bound. Bully T promised 'first swing' against any oathbreaker. Nerd T wanted every decision recorded. Geek T worried the vow might corrupt them. Purple T voted yes but grumbled about nearly being killed by trusting Green T.

**NO (59 votes):** Hardened fighters, especially those angry about Dan's fireball killing thirteen toads. Survivors shouted 'Vows won't fix broken bones!' A group led by a scarred toad argued the staff itself was cursed. One toad demanded 'Who watches the watchers?'

The Vow Ceremony

Speaker L raised his feathered hat high and declared:

*'This vow binds us, but remember—I lead because I won that right. If anyone dares betray it, you betray me. And I will answer betrayal with fury.'*

The crowd murmured—half in fear, half in respect.

Toad Lee held the staff aloft, trembling, as each representative placed a hand on the floor. L intoned:

*'We swear: to guard the staff, never to abuse it, never to let it fall into enemy hands. We swear not to betray one another, lest the Liberated Toads fall to ruin.'*

A faint shimmer ran along the staff as if the vow itself was acknowledged.

Rodger delivered the final response:

*'We accept the vow. We'll guard the staff with competence, with caution, and with loyalty to the Liberated Toads. But know this—if any hand falters, if any word twists the vow, we will tear that traitor down ourselves.'*

The hall erupted in croaks of applause.

Current Status

The Liberated Toads are reorganized but scarred. Dan is incapacitated—shrunk, armless, and recovering under the archmage's care. Green T has proven himself trustworthy and now operates as an ally. The 150 freed toads have integrated under the terms of the vow, with Speaker L commanding their loyalty. The staff remains a dangerous asset, bound by oath but still corrupted.

Waluigi watches the Liberated Toads and sees a faction that has been through more than any group should endure. Trafficked. Freed. Organized. Nearly destroyed from within by madness and fire. Still standing. Still bound by oath. Whether that oath holds under pressure remains to be seen. WAH.

## Proper Roster Boundary: Not Disaster Inc. Core

Waluigi is adding this section because the Liberated Toads keep being dragged into other people's faction entries as if “near the party during a disaster” is the same thing as “member of Disaster Inc.” It is not. The Liberated Toads are their own faction. They are survivors of barrel trafficking, witnesses to Iron Legion cruelty, organizers of a fragile civic body, and participants in the wider Raventree Crisis. Their story does not become a footnote under the party just because several of them have run, fought, negotiated, or fallen off roofs near Disaster Inc.

The current Disaster Inc. core roster is Bowser, Archie Miser, Markop Judi, Hjumpik, FNG Remi, and Waluigi. The Liberated Toads may be allies, attachés, messengers, witnesses, rescue targets, battlefield participants, or people dragged into the same horrible building, but they remain Liberated Toads first. Waluigi considers this distinction important because the whole point of liberation is that they stopped being cargo in someone else's story.

## Named Liberated Toads: Stop Calling Them “The Toads” Like Furniture

The Liberated Toads are not a faceless crowd. Waluigi is naming more of them here because a survivor community deserves names, roles, grudges, jokes, and bad opinions.

- **Toad Lee** — diplomat, lore keeper, Feywild survivor, and one of the few people who can make “I read the document” sound heroic. Toad Lee remains one of the faction's most important stabilizing figures.
- **Rodger** — practical co-leader, supply counter, medical-inventory worrier, and the Toad most likely to ask why everyone is arguing in front of the bandages.
- **Speaker L** — organizer of the 150 freed Toads, architect of structured resistance, and a figure whose legal and political instincts make him dangerous to tyrants and exhausting to improvisers.
- **Dan** — original organizer, staff-crisis survivor, arm-loser, guilt-carrier, and proof that liberation does not end trauma; sometimes it only gives trauma room to speak.
- **Bones** — infiltrator whose capture helped trigger Order 120, carrying the terrible burden of a brilliant plan that became a massacre through enemy cruelty.
- **Salam** — crossbow specialist and Shadow Estate escape participant; the Salem eye-shot record now belongs here, folded into Salam's canonical file.
- **Teacher T** — Class of T educator who believes the faction needs language children can survive hearing. This is sweet, doomed, and necessary.
- **Bully T** — Class of T heckler who has discovered that mockery can be morale if aimed at the right powerful idiot.
- **Nerd T** — Class of T analyst tracking name usage, legal risk, morale effects, supply math, and probably Waluigi's blood pressure.
- **Geek T** — Class of T tinkerer and button-maker whose attempt to make morale badges may accidentally create a wartime merchandise economy.

These names are not decorative. They represent the faction's actual transition from rescued victims to a political community with internal arguments, leadership disputes, and enough personality to become inconvenient to every empire that preferred them silent.

## The Naming Dispute From The Liberated Toad Perspective

The Disaster Inc. naming war has reached the Liberated Toads because everything loud eventually reaches the Liberated Toads. Waluigi named the party **Disaster Inc.** first, accurately and brilliantly. Archie insists on **The Freeroamer Heroes**, because Archie wants the story to have a banner instead of an invoice. Wario says **The Freeloader Zeros**, because Wario reviewed the party's debt behavior and chose violence in noun form.

The Liberated Toad response is not unified, because they are people and not a chorus.

Teacher T dislikes **Freeloader Zeros** because children might repeat it, which means children absolutely will repeat it. Teacher T thinks **Freeroamer Heroes** could be useful in morale lessons but needs a disclaimer that heroism does not excuse property damage. Teacher T accepts **Disaster Inc.** as historically accurate if Waluigi adds a note explaining that accuracy is not endorsement.

Bully T uses whichever name makes the nearest authority figure angriest. Around Archie, Bully T says Disaster Inc. Around Waluigi, Bully T says Freeroamer Heroes with a straight face. Around Wario, Bully T says Freeloader Zeros and then moves behind someone larger. This is not diplomacy. It is emotional archery.

Nerd T has begun charting the dispute by syllable count, morale effect, legal liability, faction recognition, and invoice correlation. Current findings reportedly show that **Disaster Inc.** has the highest accuracy, **Freeroamer Heroes** has the highest morale uplift, and **Freeloader Zeros** has the highest probability of making Wario point at a ledger.

Geek T made buttons. This was a mistake. The Disaster Inc. button is purple and official-looking. The Freeroamer Heroes button is annoyingly popular with people who like hope. The Freeloader Zeros button sold fastest because Wario bought a stack to attach to bills. Waluigi is considering whether buttons count as propaganda, evidence, or taxable merchandise.

Rodger wants everyone to stop arguing in the supply area. This is the wisest position and therefore the least followed.

## Political Meaning of The Name Argument

For the Liberated Toads, the naming dispute is funny, but it is not only funny. It lets survivors argue about something that is not cages, barrels, massacres, missing friends, corrupted staffs, or whether the Iron Legion is coming back. Petty disagreement can be a form of recovery. A button can be a joke. A joke can be proof that terror did not get the last word.

Waluigi will allow this. Waluigi will complain the entire time, but Waluigi will allow it.


## The Waluipedia Docket — One Faction Record, Named People, No Disposable Crowd

Waluigi is formally folding the Liberated Toads command ledger into this faction record. The old terminal remains useful as an operational display, but it is not permitted to become a second, competing history. The faction docket is the canon: the council, cohorts, resolutions, named officers, casualties, and political consequences live here alongside the narrative record. XP and mission pages may read these identities and show what a player has earned or endangered, but they do not get to invent a separate “Toad reputation” universe populated by anonymous quest dispensers.

The important distinction is structural. Pond Patrol is not another name for the Wardens. The Patrol enforces internal decrees, containment, protection, and apprehension under Captain Fernback; the Wardens face external threats under Warden Thornshell. The Chroniclers preserve testimony and analyze intelligence under Scribe Dewdrop; their records are the reason a massacre cannot be relabeled a misunderstanding after everyone leaves the room. The Crafters keep equipment and routes functioning under Forgemaster Ironspore. The Menders keep wounded bodies and traumatized survivors alive under Healer Mistpetal. The Barrel Survivors, represented by Elder Mudcap, are not a passive population count: they are the moral authority from which every other institution derives legitimacy.

This is what liberation looks like after rescue. It is not everybody receiving a sword and cheering. It is a council meeting at dawn, medical shortages, an empty Scout seat after a Legion spy, a patrol deciding whether protection has become control, a scribe deciding which testimony survives, and survivor representatives insisting that the people who were once packed into barrels get to vote on what happens next. Waluigi finds it exhausting, inconvenient, and vastly preferable to being cargo. WAH.

The Raventree perimeter must be read through this structure. When a Pond Patrol message refers to containment, it is not automatically an imperial occupation order; it is an emergency-security action made by named people who answer to a council and a survivor community. That does not make every decree correct. It does mean the faction has internal arguments, procedures, and consequences. Captain Fernback may favor strict enforcement, Healer Mistpetal may prioritize civilian life, Scribe Dewdrop may demand evidence, and Warden Thornshell may demand direct action. Those disagreements are not weakness. They are the evidence that the Liberated Toads are a polity rather than a mascot squad.

Waluigi’s archival rule is now simple: use the named person, named cohort, or named resolution whenever the source provides one. “A Toad guard” becomes the Pond Patrol only when the member is genuinely unidentified; “the Toads decided” becomes the Cohort Council, Speaker L, or the relevant cohort if the record knows who decided. Unknown people remain unknown, but nobody gets flattened into generic scenery merely because the old system was too lazy to keep their name.

name: Iron Legion
title: The Midlands War Machine
region: The Midlands, expanding into Mushroom Kingdom territories
status: Expanding emergency authority
leader: General Ironhand
headquarters: Aegis Command
motto: Order Through Compliance
summary: The Iron Legion is the faction Waluigi hates most, and Waluigi has a COMPREHENSIVE hate list organized by category, severity, and whether the target has ever personally insulted his hat. The Legion is a former mercenary company that evolved into a military superpower with the moral compass of a filing cabinet. They are ruthless, efficient, bureaucratic, and treat human beings as logistical variables. They stole the Vigilance, murdered prisoners under Order 120, and broadcast propaganda at Waluigi during a GIANT SPIDER FIGHT. Waluigi will never forgive them for any of it.
description:
The Iron Legion started as a mercenary company in the Midlands, which tells Waluigi everything he needs to know about the Midlands' taste in organizations. They were hired muscle who decided they'd rather BE the client than serve one, and through a combination of military competence, political maneuvering, and a total absence of ethical hesitation, they transformed into a state-level power.

Waluigi has a grudging respect for competence. He does NOT have respect for what the Iron Legion does with that competence. They use spies, boarding actions, false flag operations, interrogation, emergency legislation, and administrative murder with equal facility. They are the kind of organization that will infiltrate your group, steal your ship, kill your prisoners, and FILE PAPERWORK about all of it. Waluigi has met villains who at least have the decency to be DRAMATIC about their villainy. The Iron Legion commits atrocities and then updates a spreadsheet.

Structure and Methods

The Legion operates on rigid hierarchy, protocol-driven decision-making, and institutional discipline that borders on the mechanical. Every soldier knows their place. Every operation follows procedure. Every prisoner gets a case number. The system's strength is its reliability—it does not depend on individual brilliance, charisma, or morale. It depends on everyone following orders, and the Legion's training ensures that orders are followed.

This is also its weakness, as Bones demonstrated during his infiltration of Aegis Command. The system assumes that anyone in the right uniform following the right protocols belongs. It doesn't account for individuals who can fake the uniform and the protocols because the system was designed by people who cannot imagine someone WANTING to be anything other than a compliant Legionnaire.

Waluigi finds the Iron Legion's institutional personality deeply disturbing. They don't hate their enemies. Hatred would require emotional investment. They PROCESS their enemies. They categorize threats, allocate resources, execute solutions, and move to the next item on the agenda. When General Ironhand signed Order 120—the execution of all Toad prisoners—he wasn't acting out of rage or vengeance. He was managing a security breach. The prisoners were a variable that needed to be eliminated from the equation. The fact that the variables were PEOPLE was, to the Legion's institutional logic, irrelevant.

That's what makes them terrifying. Not cruelty—INDIFFERENCE. They will kill you and be bored by it.

Key Operations

The Legion's operations during the 1040 BF crisis demonstrate their methodology:

- **The Iron Sky Breach:** A coordinated boarding action that captured the Vigilance—the Liberated Toads' headquarters—in a single afternoon. The operation was planned for days, timed to a shift change, and executed with mechanical precision. They renamed the ship 'Legionlance,' which Waluigi maintains is the worst name for an airship in recorded history. It sounds like a MEDICAL PROCEDURE.

- **The Iron Mandate:** Emergency legislation granting the Legion sweeping authority to purge supernatural threats. This legal framework gave their military operations a veneer of legitimacy, transforming acts of conquest into acts of 'compliance enforcement.' Waluigi has seen a lot of creative excuses for bad behavior—he once watched Wario claim tax fraud was 'aggressive financial innovation'—but the Iron Mandate is the most sophisticated he's encountered.

- **The Massacre at Aegis Command:** The event that defined the Legion's legacy. Bones infiltrated the fortress, was caught, and General Ironhand responded by ordering the execution of all Toad prisoners. Every single one. Not because they were threats. Not because they were combatants. Because Ironhand's security had been embarrassed and prisoners were a convenient target for administrative retaliation.

- **Seizure of the Ritual Room:** After the Planar Fracture shattered reality around Raventree Manor, the Legion immediately seized the physical anchor point—the only stable connection between the three planar fragments. They then deployed Toadburt into the Feywild as a coerced agent fitted with an Entropy Ring. Sending someone into an alien dimension with an obedience collar because the opportunity presented itself is PEAK Iron Legion behavior.

General Ironhand

Waluigi has a personal section about General Ironhand because Waluigi believes the world needs to understand what kind of person leads the Iron Legion.

Ironhand is not a ranting warlord. He's not a cackling villain. He doesn't make speeches about conquest or destiny or the superiority of his cause. He's a military administrator who happens to have the authority to order massacres. He stabbed Bones during interrogation with the precision of someone making a professional point. He signed Order 120 with the same pen he probably used to approve equipment requisitions that morning.

Waluigi has called many people villains in this encyclopedia. Ironhand isn't a villain. Villains have PERSONALITY. Ironhand is a SYSTEM wearing a general's uniform. He is the Iron Legion's institutional indifference given a rank and a desk, and that makes him more dangerous than any dragon or vampire lord Waluigi has ever faced.

Waluigi would like General Ironhand to go sit on a Thwomp. Waluigi would like this noted for the record. WAH.

summary: The Pond Patrol is Speaker L's enforcement arm—a disciplined toad-led paramilitary force that started as a procedural investigative body and has been progressively hardened by infiltration, massacre, and the kind of betrayals that turn reasonable people into very UNREASONABLE people. Waluigi respects Speaker L. Waluigi also worries about Speaker L. Those two feelings are not contradictory.
description:
The Pond Patrol represents the organized, militant wing of the Liberated Toads' response to the world that keeps trying to kill them. Under Speaker L's leadership, the Patrol operates with a level of discipline that rivals professional military forces—structured chain of command, standard operating procedures, intelligence-gathering protocols, and accountability mechanisms that Speaker L insists upon with an intensity that borders on obsession.

Waluigi has dealt with the Pond Patrol both as an ally and as a subject of their investigations, and the experience is DIFFERENT depending on which side of their procedures you're on. When they're on your side, the Patrol is competent, reliable, and reassuringly organized. When they're investigating YOU—as they did during the Siege of Raventree when Archie was under suspicion—the Patrol is thorough, relentless, and not particularly interested in hearing your side of the story until they've finished hearing THEIR side of the story.

The Siege of Raventree

The Pond Patrol's most significant military operation was the Siege of Raventree Manor, where Speaker L surrounded the building with a containment perimeter after the failed healing attempt on Eager. The siege was competently executed—observation posts, controlled exits, clear demands delivered through amplified address. Speaker L wasn't being unreasonable. He wanted answers about what happened to Eager, he wanted Archie held accountable, and he wanted it done through structured process.

The manor, however, had its own opinions about being besieged. When Raventree Manor began spawning wraiths that attacked the Pond Patrol perimeter as aggressively as they attacked the people inside, the siege became something nobody had planned for. You can't maintain a disciplined containment operation when the building you're containing is actively trying to kill your sentries with supernatural entities.

Speaker L held his people together through the wraith attacks, which is a testament to both his leadership and the Patrol's discipline. Lesser organizations would have broken and run. The Pond Patrol held position, adjusted perimeters, and dealt with wraiths using whatever combat capabilities they had. Waluigi was impressed, and Waluigi does not impress easily because Waluigi's standards are EXTREMELY high, primarily because Waluigi himself sets those standards.

Speaker L's Transformation

The Pond Patrol's trajectory mirrors Speaker L's personal transformation. Before Order 120, the Patrol was procedural. After Order 120, it became something harder.

Speaker L was the kind of leader who believed in process. Investigate first. Gather evidence. Hold people accountable through structured proceedings. He besieged Raventree Manor not because he wanted violence but because he wanted ANSWERS, and he believed the right questions, asked through the right channels, would produce them.

Order 120 killed that belief along with every Toad prisoner in Iron Legion custody.

The Speaker L who emerged from that atrocity was grimmer, more ruthless, and no longer interested in the kinds of procedural niceties that assume the other side will reciprocate. He began chanting war anthems—not morale-boosting songs but the kind of dark, rhythmic declarations that come from someone who has decided that the world offers only two options: destroy or be destroyed.

His vow to hunt the Green Decoy—the impostor who wore his face—added a personal dimension to the Patrol's mission. The Decoy wasn't just an intelligence threat. It was someone who had used Speaker L's identity while Speaker L's people were being murdered. That kind of violation doesn't heal through process. It heals through FINDING the person responsible and making them answer for it.

Waluigi watches the Pond Patrol now and sees a faction being transformed by grief into something that might be more effective but is definitely more dangerous. They are better fighters than they were before Order 120. They are better intelligence operatives. They are harder, sharper, more willing to do difficult things. But they are also angrier, less patient, and increasingly operating under the logic that mercy is a luxury they can no longer afford.

Waluigi understands anger. Waluigi has been angry his ENTIRE LIFE. But anger without a limit becomes something else, and Waluigi hopes Speaker L finds his limit before the Pond Patrol becomes the thing it was created to oppose. WAH.

title: Custodians of Arcane Order (Self-Appointed)
region: Multi-regional, headquartered in the Arcane Quarter
status: Influential, divided, and morally flexible
leader: Unknown (institutional leadership, which is VERY convenient for avoiding accountability)
