motto: Knowledge Is Responsibility (allegedly)
summary: The Mages' Guild is the kind of institution that presents itself as the responsible adult in the room while actively making the room MORE dangerous through 'research.' They study threats that their studying makes worse, they track people with magical surveillance badges, they maintain null cages for containing supernatural entities, and they have clashed repeatedly with Archie Miser, which is the ONE thing about them Waluigi finds relatable because Waluigi ALSO clashes with Archie, though Waluigi's clashes involve less bureaucracy and more shouting.
description:
Waluigi has a complicated relationship with the Mages' Guild. On one hand, they possess genuine expertise in magical theory, planar mechanics, and supernatural containment that has proven valuable during the Raventree crisis. Agent L, their primary field operative in the campaign, is competent, practical, and has on multiple occasions done genuinely heroic things. Waluigi respects Agent L as an individual.

On the other hand, the INSTITUTION is a different animal entirely. The Mages' Guild treats people the way mathematicians treat variables—as elements in an equation to be solved. They investigate phenomena with a clinical detachment that fails to account for the fact that the phenomena are happening TO PEOPLE. They study planar instability in ways that may worsen the instability. They monitor individuals with magical tracking badges without necessarily informing those individuals that they're being tracked. They maintain null cages—containment devices designed to hold supernatural entities—and seem more interested in what they can LEARN from the contained entities than in whether the containment is ethical.

Waluigi finds the Guild's moral positioning EXHAUSTING. They claim to be custodians of arcane order while conducting experiments that threaten to DISORDER everything further. They present themselves as neutral arbiters of magical law while pursuing institutional agendas that benefit the Guild's power and influence. They lecture Archie Miser about responsible magic use while their own research programs push boundaries that responsible practitioners would never approach.

Relationship with Archie Miser

The Guild and Archie have a history that predates the current crisis. Archie's magical approach—instinctive, volatile, fire-oriented, and conducted with the caution of someone who has never read a safety manual—is everything the Guild officially opposes. His confession to Guild authorities (the specifics of which Waluigi was not privy to) created a complicated legal and institutional entanglement that has never been fully resolved.

The Onyx Hand's acquittal of Archie through their own tribunal further damaged the Guild's relationship with both Archie and the vampiric power structure. The Guild viewed the acquittal as a direct challenge to their authority—a supernatural faction overruling Guild jurisdiction in matters of magical misconduct. This institutional grievance has colored the Guild's approach to the Raventree crisis, where vampiric, fey, and other supernatural powers are active players.

Waluigi thinks the Guild-Archie conflict is essentially two control freaks arguing about who gets to control the same chaotic situation, except one control freak uses fireballs and the other uses paperwork. Neither approach has produced stability. Both have produced FIRES, metaphorical and literal.

Role in the Raventree Crisis

The Guild's involvement in the Raventree Manor situation has been both helpful and troubling. Their expertise in planar mechanics has provided critical theoretical frameworks for understanding the Planar Fracture—what happened, why, and potentially how to fix it. Without Guild research, the scattered fragments of Disaster Inc. would have even less understanding of the dimensions they're trapped in.

But the Guild is also STUDYING the fracture. Actively. With instruments and researchers and the kind of academic enthusiasm that prioritizes understanding over urgency. People are trapped in hostile dimensions—Waluigi was in the FEYWILD dealing with fairy riddles while the Guild was presumably writing research papers about the Feywild's fascinating planar mechanics. The disconnect between 'people are suffering' and 'what an interesting phenomenon' is the Guild's fundamental moral failure, and Waluigi doubts they'll ever recognize it because recognizing it would require them to view people as something other than data points.

Agent L

Agent L deserves separate mention because Agent L is better than the institution they serve. Practical where the Guild is theoretical. Engaged where the Guild is detached. Willing to get their hands dirty in ways that Guild policy neither explicitly authorizes nor explicitly forbids, which gives Agent L the operational flexibility to actually HELP people rather than just study their problems.

Waluigi suspects Agent L has internal conflicts about serving an institution whose priorities don't always align with doing the right thing. Waluigi recognizes this because Waluigi has spent his entire life associated with groups—Wario's Enterprise, various sports teams, the general category of 'villains'—whose priorities don't always align with his own. The difference between being PART of something and AGREEING with something is a distinction Waluigi understands intimately. WAH.

## The Archie Connection
Archie Miser is a target of the Guild's interest because of his unique metaphysical properties—specifically "what bleeds from him." This likely refers to his connection to the Star Bits or the "blaze" that he carries. The Guild views Archie as a resource to be harvested or a leak to be plugged.

name: Peach Loyalists
title: The Ruthless Restorationists
region: Mushroom Kingdom
status: Resurgent and uncompromising
leader: Captain Toadette
headquarters: Toad Town (seized), Bramblehaven (captured)
motto: For the Crown, Whatever the Cost
summary: The Peach Loyalists are the faction that makes Waluigi most uncomfortable, and Waluigi has been uncomfortable in a LOT of situations. They fight for Princess Peach's memory and legacy, which SOUNDS noble until you see HOW they fight—with absolute ruthlessness, no quarter given, and a willingness to execute surrendering troops that would make the Iron Legion wince. Captain Toadette is the scariest person in the Mushroom Kingdom who isn't a dragon or a dimensional horror, and Waluigi says that as someone who has arm-wrestled Bowser.
description:
The Peach Loyalists exist because Princess Peach is dead and the circumstances of her death remain unresolved. That combination—grief and mystery—is DANGEROUS. It creates the kind of devotion that doesn't ask whether its methods are justified because the cause is too sacred to question. Waluigi has seen this pattern before on a smaller scale (sports fans who riot when their team loses) but never with this level of military capability and willingness to commit atrocities.

The faction is driven by two objectives: uncovering the truth behind Princess Peach's assassination and restoring her cause to dominance in the Mushroom Kingdom. Scouts like Embercap and Mistveil pursue intelligence leads with dedication that borders on obsession, investigating Peach's private chambers, past relationships, and the political networks that surrounded her. The information they've uncovered—including revelations from a gala event and secrets found in Peach's personal quarters—has deepened the mystery rather than resolving it.

Command Structure

The Loyalists operate with military precision under a clear chain of command:

**Captain Toadette** stands at the top—tactician, executioner, and symbol of the cause. She plans operations meticulously and executes them without mercy. Her reputation alone causes enemy garrisons to consider surrender, though surrendering TO Toadette is not advisable.

**Embercap** serves as Field Commander, leading assaults from the front. His crimson plume cuts through battlefield smoke like a wound, and his presence steadies wavering troops. At Bramblehaven, he was among the first over the walls, hammer cleaving through defenders as he gained the parapet.

**Mistveil** now governs Toad Town as Interim Governor, managing the provisional government while Toadette focuses on military campaigns. She was severely wounded during the Bramblehaven assault—struck by arcane frost and thrown from a ladder—but recovered under Dewdrop's care.

**Dewdrop** is Chief Medic, commanding the healers who work frantically behind the lines. At Bramblehaven, she shouted orders through thunder and cannon fire, dragging wounded soldiers to safety even as more fell frozen mid-climb.

**Big R** is the faction's heavy assault specialist—a living siege tower who goes first up every ladder and throws captured tanks through castle gates.

Captain Toadette

Waluigi needs to talk about Captain Toadette because Captain Toadette is the faction's beating heart and its sharpest blade.

Toadette is not a cackling villain. She's not a ranting fanatic. She's WORSE than both of those things because she's COMPETENT. She plans operations meticulously—the Fall of Bramblehaven was a masterpiece of siege tactics, with sappers tunneling overnight, simultaneous three-pronged assaults, and coordinated breach teams that took a fortified bastion in a single day. That level of military planning requires intelligence, patience, and skill.

She also executed surrendering garrison troops and shot one of her own sergeants for suggesting a tactical retreat.

The combination of tactical brilliance and moral absolutism is what makes Toadette dangerous. She's not cruel for the sake of cruelty. She genuinely believes that Peach's cause demands total commitment, and total commitment means total war. No prisoners. No retreats. No compromises. Everything offered on the altar of a dead princess's legacy.

Waluigi has met Peach. Waluigi has COMPETED against Peach in sports events. Princess Peach was gracious, kind, and had excellent sportsmanship even when Waluigi was CLEARLY being cheated by the referees. Waluigi does not believe for one second that Princess Peach would have approved of what is being done in her name. But the Loyalists aren't asking Peach's opinion. They're asking her MEMORY, and memory doesn't talk back.

The Siege of Bramblehaven

The assault on Bramblehaven began beneath a sky thick with smoke and rain. The old fort-town—a proud Fawthful bastion nestled among thorny hills—stood defiant, its towers crowned in emerald banners, its ramparts bristling with cannons and crossbows. Behind those walls waited a garrison of hardened Fawthful veterans, absolutely certain their faith would carry them through.

Toadette's horn sounded at dawn, rallying an ocean of soldiers. Their ranks stretched to the horizon—thousands of armored toads advancing through mud and shattered earth. When Toadette raised her arm, the ladders went up all at once—a forest of wooden spines stabbing toward the walls.

Big R was first to climb, roaring defiance as arrows and fire rained down. Embercap followed, his hammer cleaving through defenders. Mistveil scaled beside them until a burst of arcane frost struck her full in the chest, hurling her into the mud below. Dewdrop's medics rushed forward, dragging the wounded to safety as more soldiers fell frozen mid-climb.

A Fawthful warlock unleashed a wave of frost that froze twenty Loyalists solid—silent statues of ice and valor. But a toad from the lower ranks leapt the final rung and drove his dagger into the warlock's back, ending the spell and the stalemate both.

As night fell, Toadette sounded the horn again. The ladders rose anew, rebuilt from splinters and blood. Big R hurled a captured tank through the inner gate; the explosion tore the heart out of Bramblehaven's keep. Surrender came late—and it was not accepted. Even as defenders threw down their arms, the Loyalists pressed forward. A toad screamed 'They're dead! Stop attacking!' but the advance continued.

By dawn, Bramblehaven was ash and ruin. Heavy casualties on both sides, but the Loyalists held the field. Among the bodies, a guard feigning death rose to strike one final blow—killing a young toad before being cut down. The survivor gasped 'We got the intel' before collapsing.

Toadette's Victory Speech

Standing atop the crumbled battlements, Toadette wiped dust from her cheek and raised her voice above the roar of celebration:

*'Today, the Fawthful fall—not by luck, but by courage! You all climbed these walls when others said it couldn't be done. You fought not for conquest, but for every toad still chained, every friend still waiting for a dawn like this. Remember this sight—Bramblehaven stands with us now, and the world will know: no wall can hold back a free people!'*

The toads erupted into cheers, their voices echoing across the ruined fortress as the sun broke through the smoke.

Current Holdings

The Loyalists now control Toad Town under Mistveil's provisional government and Bramblehaven as a forward operating base. Intelligence recovered from the garrison—troop movements, supply chains, Fawthful communications—has accelerated their subsequent campaigns. The no-quarter policy has created a deterrent effect: two subsequent Fawthful garrisons surrendered without fighting rather than face Toadette's methods. They surrendered to OTHER factions, of course. Nobody surrenders to Toadette.

Waluigi watches the Loyalists and sees a faction that has transformed grief into a weapon. They are effective. They are terrifying. And they are convinced that everything they do serves a righteous cause. WAH.

## Civil War Role

The Peach Loyalists are not merely a faction with strong feelings. They are a restorationist military regime operating inside the Mushroom Kingdom Civil War. Their claim is moral rather than procedural: the Regency inherited a murder, therefore the Regency's paperwork is contaminated. This gives the Loyalists enormous emotional force and very little patience for compromise.

They control territory through disciplined violence, martyr memory, and the belief that Peach's cause must be restored by action. Their weakness is the same as their strength: certainty. A regime that never doubts itself can move quickly. It can also execute prisoners and call the speed justice.

name: Fawful's Forces
title: The Cackling Menace
region: Mushroom Kingdom (contested, shrinking)
status: Weakened and losing territory; a 2 Aethel field report describes sacrifice preparations for a dragon-linked ritual, with location and outcome unknown.
leader: Fawful
headquarters: Unknown (primary holdings under pressure)
motto: I HAVE FURY! (Fawful's words, not Waluigi's)
summary: Fawful's Forces are the occupying army of a cackling megalomaniac who talks about himself in the third person, which Waluigi finds deeply irritating for reasons he cannot fully articulate. Waluigi ALSO sometimes refers to himself in the third person but Waluigi does it with STYLE and GRAVITAS. Fawful does it while ranting about 'mustard of doom' and making everyone in earshot wish they were somewhere else. His forces are losing ground across the Mushroom Kingdom, partly because the Peach Loyalists are carving through them and partly because working for Fawful is presumably exhausting. A 2 Aethel Bones report adds an unverified dragon-linked ritual and sacrifice preparation; it does not establish a completed summon or a formal relationship with the Emerald Enclave.
description:
Fawful is one of those enemies who would be funny if he weren't also genuinely dangerous. His speech patterns are incomprehensible, his plans are grandiose to the point of absurdity, and his behavior suggests a relationship with sanity that can best be described as 'long-distance.' But he has an army. He holds territory. He has occupied significant portions of the Mushroom Kingdom through a combination of technological superiority, mechanical minions, and the sheer overwhelming ENERGY of a being who never, ever stops.

Waluigi has encountered Fawful peripherally and found the experience deeply unpleasant. Not because Fawful is threatening in person—though he IS—but because trying to have a conversation with Fawful is like trying to read a book that's on fire. The words are there but the medium is hostile.

Territorial Holdings

Fawful's forces held significant territory in the Mushroom Kingdom at the start of the 1040 BF crisis, including the fortified bastion of Bramblehaven. His occupation was characterized by mechanical efficiency—automated defenses, construct patrols, and garrison troops who operated under Fawful's... unique... command style.

The Fall of Bramblehaven was the first major crack in Fawful's territorial control. The garrison that defended the bastion fought well—three hours defending the central keep against overwhelming numbers, creative use of urban terrain, and genuine courage in the face of certain death. Waluigi respects the garrison's determination even though he has no love for Fawful himself. The soldiers defending Bramblehaven were fighting for their position, their comrades, and their survival. The fact that their ultimate commander is a cackling gremlin doesn't diminish THEIR courage.

After Bramblehaven fell, Fawful was forced to consolidate. He abandoned smaller outposts to reinforce core holdings, which created a cascade of territorial losses as opportunistic factions—local groups, independent operators, anyone who saw undefended ground and wanted it—moved into the vacuum. Fawful's empire is shrinking, and each loss makes the next loss more likely because fewer garrisons means fewer reinforcement options means more vulnerability.

Assessment

Waluigi expects Fawful's forces to continue losing ground unless Fawful produces one of his characteristic dramatic reversals—a superweapon, a dimensional portal, a mechanical army upgrade, or some other escalation that nobody saw coming. Fawful has a history of pulling absurd solutions from seemingly impossible situations, usually while cackling. Underestimating him would be a mistake. Overestimating him would also be a mistake. The correct estimation of Fawful is 'unpredictable and dangerous,' which is coincidentally also the correct estimation of Waluigi, except Waluigi is ALSO handsome. WAH.

## Civil War Role

Fawful's Forces function as an occupation regime inside the civil war. Fawful does not claim to be the lawful heir of Peach or the moral restorer of the throne. He controls what he can fortify, mechanize, mutate, and defend with enough spectacle that everyone remembers his name even while wishing they did not.

His occupation of Peach's Castle makes him more than a raider. A castle is infrastructure, symbol, and weapon. Fawful turns all three into a war machine. Waluigi considers him ridiculous, but ridiculous is not harmless. Sometimes ridiculous has artillery.


## 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — Bones's Report
Bones's field account places Fawful directing Bean forces, a mustard-spraying clockwork drone, and preparations for a sacrifice tied by witnesses to a dragon-summoning plan. Bones escaped before the ritual's outcome. A dragon arrived later at an unnamed goblin camp, but no evidence establishes that the ritual brought it there. The Emerald Enclave is named by two people in the field report; no formal enemy, alliance, or territorial status is assigned here.

name: Wario's Enterprise
title: Profit Over Everything
region: Wherever there's money, chaos, or preferably both
status: Thriving (chaos is GREAT for business)
leader: Wario (CEO, CFO, and Chief Destruction Officer)
headquarters: Mobile — Wario goes where the profit goes
motto: If it's not nailed down, it's inventory. If it IS nailed down, bring a crowbar.
summary: Wario's Enterprise is the greatest business venture in the history of commerce and Waluigi will not be accepting alternative opinions on this matter. Founded and operated by Wario—Waluigi's business partner, occasional ally, and the only person Waluigi trusts with money (because Wario loves money too much to waste it on betrayal)—the Enterprise operates on a simple principle: every crisis is an opportunity, every opportunity has a price, and that price should be paid to Wario.
description:
Waluigi is going to write about Wario's Enterprise with a disclosure: Waluigi is a MEMBER of Wario's Enterprise. Waluigi is Wario's business partner, field operative, and the person who handles the parts of the operation that require HEIGHT, AGILITY, and CHARM, which is to say most of the important parts.

This means Waluigi is biased. Waluigi is biased about EVERYTHING in this encyclopedia, but he's ESPECIALLY biased about this. Consider yourselves warned.

Business Model

Wario's Enterprise operates on a business model that most economists would describe as 'criminal' and Wario would describe as 'innovative.' The Enterprise deals in treasure acquisition, debt collection, contraband distribution, mercenary contracting, opportunistic logistics, demolition services, and whatever else presents itself when the world is falling apart.

The key insight behind the Enterprise—and Waluigi gives Wario full credit for this—is that CHAOS IS PROFITABLE. When empires clash, when factions collapse, when buildings explode and dimensions shatter, there are ALWAYS opportunities for someone fast enough and flexible enough to grab them. Organized factions are too rigid to adapt. Ideological factions are too principled to capitalize. Wario's Enterprise has neither rigidity nor principles, which makes it the most adaptable organization in the setting.

Wario maintains a debt ledger that tracks obligations owed to the Enterprise by individuals across multiple factions. The ledger is legendary. It contains entries for major political figures, military commanders, criminal bosses, and at least one dragon (now deceased). The debts are not always monetary—Wario trades in favors, information, access, and anything else that has value. The ledger gives the Enterprise leverage that is entirely disproportionate to its size, because owing Wario a favor is like having a persistent itch in a place you can't reach. It never goes away and it's ALWAYS uncomfortable.

The Tome Heist

One of the Enterprise's most notable operations was the theft of valuable magical tomes—an operation that brought Wario into direct conflict with parties who did NOT appreciate having their libraries raided. Waluigi will not provide details about the theft because Waluigi was involved and Waluigi has been advised by himself to maintain operational security. What Waluigi WILL say is that the tomes were extremely valuable, the theft was executed with characteristic Enterprise efficiency, and the consequences are still playing out.

Wario vs. The World

Wario is not a complicated person. He wants money. He wants treasure. He wants to WIN, where 'winning' is defined as having more money and treasure than he had yesterday. His motivations are transparent, his methods are direct, and his appetite for wealth is BOTTOMLESS.

Waluigi loves working with Wario because Wario is HONEST about what he is. In a world full of factions that dress up their ambitions in noble language—the Iron Legion's 'Order Through Compliance,' the Peach Loyalists' 'For the Crown,' the Mages' Guild's 'Knowledge Is Responsibility'—Wario just says 'I want money' and then goes and GETS money. There's a purity to it that Waluigi finds refreshing.

Also, Wario has never cut off anyone's finger to impress a vampire, which puts him ahead of CERTAIN party members in Waluigi's estimation.

Waluigi's Role

Waluigi serves as the Enterprise's primary field operative for operations requiring stealth, agility, magical capability, and what Wario calls 'the weird stuff'—supernatural encounters, planar navigation, and situations where punching something isn't sufficient. Waluigi brings ice magic, arcane rays, athletic prowess, and a MAGNIFICENT sense of personal style to an organization that would otherwise be entirely about a large man in yellow punching things and taking their coins.

Waluigi is the Enterprise's sophistication. Waluigi is its FINESSE. Without Waluigi, Wario's Enterprise would be a blunt instrument. WITH Waluigi, it is a blunt instrument that also has a REALLY SHARP EDGE. WAH!

name: Onyx Hand
title: The Night Court
region: Shadowfell (Shadow Estate), with political reach into the physical world
status: Destabilized — succession crisis active, portal circle occupied, and Disaster Inc. now has all four portal artifacts
leader: Orangus Cornelius (shot with silver, recovering uncertain), Vivian Corvinarus (active claimant, HOSTILE)
headquarters: The Shadow Estate, Shadowfell
motto: Blood Remembers
summary:
The Onyx Hand is a vampiric power bloc that was ALREADY in crisis after Green T shot Orangus Cornelius with a silver bullet at the infamous dinner party. Now it's WORSE. Vivian Corvinarus—who spent weeks hiding as a harmless thrall named 'Vivesna'—has dropped the disguise and gone active, hunting party members through the Shadow Estate's corridors with magic that ignores Shadowfell suppression. The succession has gone from cold war to hot war. Waluigi was not present at their dinner party—he was in the FEYWILD—but the situation has deteriorated so dramatically that even fairy court politics seem manageable by comparison.

Recent update: the Shadow Estate’s control problem has become an exit problem. The Mirror of True Reflection has been restored, all four portal artifacts are secured, and the master-bedroom portal circle is occupied by Tanukiburt, real injured Toadburt, and Mystic Morel while Lyranth and Vaxillus pursue the escaping party.
description:
The Onyx Hand operates at the intersection of criminal authority, supernatural power, and the kind of aristocratic tradition that uses the word 'tradition' to justify murder. They first appeared in direct political relevance when an Onyx Hand tribunal acquitted Archie Miser of magical misconduct charges, overruling the Mages' Guild's jurisdiction.

In the Shadowfell, the Onyx Hand's power is concentrated in the Shadow Estate—the dark reflection of Raventree Manor. The estate operates as both residence and court, a place where vampiric nobility conduct politics through formal dinners, blood rituals, hostage etiquette, and the casual violence that vampires apparently consider good table manners.

The Shadow Estate Dinner

The dinner party that culminated in Orangus Cornelius being shot with a silver bullet was the Onyx Hand's defining moment, and everything Waluigi knows about it makes him grateful he was in the Feywild instead.

The vote tradition—forcing guests to choose which attendee would be killed—is psychological domination disguised as a party game. Archie navigated it under his Darman Knightly cover. Green T sat at the children's table plotting armed rebellion. Bowser sat wherever Bowser wanted.

Green T's silver bullet forced a succession crisis. What nobody realized at the time was that the succession was already being MANAGED from the inside.

The Vivian Revelation

The Onyx Hand's succession crisis has escalated from political maneuvering to active violence.

Vivian Corvinarus operated inside the Shadow Estate for WEEKS under the thrall disguise 'Vivesna.' During that time, he mapped the manor, catalogued its defenses, identified key personnel, and positioned himself for the succession—all while appearing to be a harmless servant.

Waluigi previously described Vivian's strategy as 'effective but incredibly boring—where is the showmanship? Where is the TENNIS?' Waluigi retracts this assessment entirely. Vivian was not being boring. Vivian was being PATIENT, and patience combined with triple identities and Shadowfell-immune death magic is the OPPOSITE of boring.

Vivian has now dropped the thrall disguise and begun hunting. His corridor ambush of Markop and Bowser demonstrated capabilities that rewrite the Shadow Estate's threat landscape:

- **Crimson energy beam** that bypasses Shadowfell magic suppression
- **Tactical training** with both physical weapons and magical combat
- **Supernatural pain tolerance** — laughed while bleeding from an axe wound
- **Intimate knowledge** of the entire Shadow Estate from weeks of reconnaissance

The combination of stealth intelligence and offensive capability makes Vivian the most dangerous individual currently in the Shadow Estate. More dangerous than Orangus Cornelius, who is wounded. More dangerous than Kryn, who is injured. More dangerous than the party, who can't use offensive magic in this dimension.

The Succession Now

The Onyx Hand's power structure is fracturing in real-time:

**Orangus Cornelius** — Recovering from silver poisoning. Status uncertain. If he survives, the succession remains contested. If he dies, the Shadow thread of the Three Threads prophecy may sever.

**Kryn Corvinarus** — Injured. Position in the succession unclear. Potentially a secondary target for Vivian.

**Vivian Corvinarus** — Active. Hostile. Has dropped all pretense and is pursuing the Heir title through violence. Carries a necromancer's wand (now lost to the party) and casts magic that ignores planar rules.

**The Guards and Court** — Caught between loyalties. Some serve Orangus. Some may secretly support Vivian. Some are just trying to survive a power transition in a vampire court, which historically involves significant quantities of dust and screaming.

The Three Threads prophecy warns that cutting any thread unravels the tapestry. If Vivian kills Orangus and seizes the Shadow thread by force rather than legitimate succession, the metaphysical consequences could worsen the Planar Fracture.

The Onyx Hand isn't just experiencing a leadership change. It's experiencing a structural crisis that could BREAK REALITY FURTHER.

The Corvinarus Connection

The Onyx Hand is intimately connected to House Corvinarus—the ancient family whose members exist across multiple dimensions. Orangus Cornelius is the Shadowfell branch. Lady Aurelian Corvinarus is the Feywild branch. The Oracle may be connected to a third branch.

The family is less a conventional lineage and more a metaphysical structure—a house that exists across planes, each branch reflecting different aspects of the same fundamental power. The Onyx Hand's troubles don't just destabilize vampire politics—they destabilize the ENTIRE Corvinarus power structure.

Vivian's ambitions, if realized through violence, could collapse this structure entirely. And a collapsed Corvinarus structure means a collapsed dimensional framework means the Planar Fracture gets WORSE.

Waluigi's official position on the Onyx Hand: the situation has deteriorated from 'dangerous political intrigue' to 'active hunting ground with reality-scale consequences.' Stay away from their dinner parties. Stay away from their corridors. Stay away from anyone in red robes who laughs when you hit them.

And if you MUST deal with the Onyx Hand, bring silver. Bring divine magic. And bring someone who can match Vivian's death beam, because Waluigi doesn't know anyone who can.

WAH.

## Interest in Archie Miser
Recent intelligence suggests the Onyx Hand (often referred to simply as "The Hand" in cryptic correspondence) views Archie Miser as a person of interest for "what he might become." This implies they see Archie as a potential asset—or a potential threat—whose development is tied to the Shadowfell's entropic nature. They are actively monitoring his "blaze" and may be seeking to recruit or consume his potential.

name: Tea Leaf Syndicate
title: The Broken Tea Table
region: Formerly the Vigilance
status: Destroyed as an organization; Green T now allied with Liberated Toads
leader: Green T (surviving, now allied with Liberated Toads)
headquarters: Formerly a converted cargo hold on the Vigilance (had nice curtains)
motto: Every problem can be discussed over tea (no longer applicable)
affiliation: Former underworld networks; Green T now aligned with Liberated Toads
summary: The Tea Leaf Syndicate was the classiest criminal organization Waluigi has ever encountered. They served excellent tea. They had tasteful décor. They conducted their criminal enterprises with aesthetic sensibility. Then Archie Miser fireballed their headquarters, Roger poisoned their enforcer until he exploded, and the entire organization collapsed. Green T survived, lost everything, and has since proven himself trustworthy to the Liberated Toads through sacrifice during the Vigilance Crisis. Waluigi mourns the Chamomile Midnight blend most of all.
description:
The Tea Leaf Syndicate operated aboard the Vigilance as a smuggling, protection, and distribution network disguised—thinly but ELEGANTLY—as a tea trading operation. Their headquarters was a converted cargo hold furnished with actual tea sets, comfortable seating, and curtains that suggested someone in the organization had genuine interior design sense. Waluigi noticed the curtains. Waluigi ALWAYS notices curtains.

The Syndicate's leadership structure centered on two figures: Green T, the enigmatic boss who ran a criminal empire with the demeanor of someone hosting a garden party; and Earl Grey, the primary enforcer whose physical capabilities and, as it turned out, EXPLOSIVE physiology made him one of the most dangerous individuals aboard the ship.

The Tea Party Incident

The Syndicate's downfall began with the Tea Party Incident—Archie Miser's catastrophic attempt at diplomacy that ended with a fireball in a cargo hold. The blast killed most of the Syndicate's combat personnel and destroyed the organization's ability to project force.

The Syndicate Showdown

The final confrontation came at the Vigilance's mid-deck marketplace. Green T revealed his giant transformation—a capability that nobody had suspected. Earl Grey's death was spectacular: Roger's poisoned dagger interacted with something in Earl Grey's biology, and the enforcer DETONATED.

The explosion ended the Tea Leaf Syndicate as a functioning entity.

Green T's Redemption

Green T's subsequent career has been extraordinary. He was pulled into a mirror dimension during the Siege of Raventree. He reappeared in the Shadowfell. He attended the Shadow Estate dinner party, was insulted to the children's table, and used the insult as cover to shoot a vampire lord with a silver bullet.

But his most significant transformation came during the Vigilance Crisis. When Dan went mad and threatened to consume the souls of the Liberated Toads, Green T acted. He attacked Dan, was flung into the mob, was beaten by the crowd, yet still crawled back to negotiate. He successfully wrested the cursed staff from Dan—even chopping off Dan's arm to do so.

When Toad Lee seized the staff from Green T, instead of demanding it back, Green T accepted the outcome. Toad Lee acknowledged his sacrifice: 'You proved yourself trustworthy.'

Green T now operates as an ally of the Liberated Toads—no longer a crime lord, no longer an independent operator, but someone who has earned trust through blood and sacrifice. Waluigi has developed enormous respect for him. Green T is proof that being underestimated is a weapon, and Waluigi—who has been underestimated his ENTIRE LIFE—finds that deeply inspiring. WAH.

name: House Corvinarus
title: The Architects of the Grafting
region: Raventree Manor and its dimensional reflections (Past, Present, and Future)
status: Actively Unraveling — Shadow Estate portal route contested after the Mirror of True Reflection was restored
leader: Disputed — Orangus Cornelius (Shadowfell, wounded), Lady Aurelian (Feywild), Vivian (Active Claimant, HOSTILE), Darius (Historical/Sanctum)
headquarters: Raventree Manor (All iterations) and the Planar Sanctum
motto: Three Manors, Three Lords, Three Threads
summary:
House Corvinarus is not a family so much as a cosmic structural failure that has started ACTIVELY trying to kill people. They are at the center of the Raventree Manor crisis, the Planar Fracture, and a succession war that has gone from cold political maneuvering to Vivian Corvinarus hunting party members through corridors with death magic. Waluigi has dealt with Wario's family reunions—which usually involve property damage and garlic poisoning—but the Corvinarus family drama literally broke time and space, and now the person trying to claim the inheritance is doing it with a crimson death beam. Waluigi hates them MORE than before, which Waluigi did not think was possible.

Recent update: the Shadow Estate branch of the crisis now centers on the master-bedroom portal circle. The party has all four artifacts, including the restored Mirror of True Reflection, but Tanukiburt, Toadburt, and Mystic Morel are at the route home. Waluigi considers this family’s architecture personally offensive.
description:
House Corvinarus is the thread connecting almost every supernatural crisis in the campaign. Their manor is not three separate buildings, but ONE building existing across dimensional boundaries and different points in TIME. Understanding the Corvinarus family requires accepting that conventional concepts like 'here,' 'there,' 'past,' and 'future' are completely broken in their presence.

Recent intelligence has made things WORSE.

The Grafting (Year 988 BF)

Through ghostly visions and Lady Aurelian's diary, the origin of the bloodline split has been discovered.

In 988, an event known as 'The Grafting' took place. An orange-robed Corvinarus cut their own palm over a dragon egg. The egg SCREAMED—'like winter wind through crystal.' This ritual bound the Corvinarus bloodline to draconic power, creating an heir to 'both vine and scale.'

Most disturbing: **the Iron Legion was there.** Legion observers watched the blood magic, nodding in approval because they believed it offered 'the promise of control.' Bureaucrats funding blood magic to create a weaponized heir. Waluigi is disgusted but not surprised.

The Grafting explains WHY the Corvinarus bloodline is so dangerous. They're not just vampires. They're not just aristocrats. They carry DRACONIC LEGACY in their blood. Lady Aurelian has elemental resistances. Vivian apparently has magic that ignores dimensional suppression. The dragon egg's scream echoes through every generation.

The Three Threads Prophecy

The family's metaphysical law: *'Three manors, three lords, three threads. Cut one, and the tapestry unravels.'*

This is why the Planar Fracture is so devastating. Orangus Cornelius (Shadowfell) represents one thread. Lady Aurelian (Feywild) represents another. The third is tied to the physical world or the Deep Mirror.

The problem is now ACUTE: Vivian is actively trying to cut the Shadow thread. If he kills Orangus and seizes control by force, the thread doesn't transfer—it BREAKS. Vivian apparently either doesn't know this, doesn't believe it, or doesn't care.

Waluigi appreciates a good tapestry, but hinging the survival of the universe on a family of arrogant vampires with draconic blood magic while one of them HUNTS THE OTHERS is terrible structural engineering.

The Succession Crisis (ESCALATED)

The family is tearing itself apart. What was previously a cold political standoff has become active warfare:

**In the Shadowfell:** Vivian has dropped his 'Vivesna' thrall disguise and gone hunting. His corridor ambush of Markop and Bowser demonstrated Shadowfell-immune crimson magic, tactical training, and the ability to laugh while bleeding from an axe wound. He is no longer waiting for Orangus to die. He is MAKING it happen.

**Orangus Cornelius** remains wounded from Green T's silver bullet. His recovery is uncertain. The guards around him are caught between protecting their lord and potentially backing a new claimant who has demonstrated terrifying capabilities.

**Kryn Corvinarus** is injured and potentially a secondary target. The succession has become a hunting ground.

**In the Feywild:** Lady Aurelian is actively trying to lock down her timeline (stuck in Year 722 of the 'Eternal Bloom'). She views other dimensions as lost causes and is attempting to sever the planes to save her own present. Her draconic nature—vertical pupils hidden behind illusions, elemental resistances—makes her far more dangerous than her 'delicate fey hostess' persona suggests.

Vivian's Transformation

Waluigi previously described Vivian's strategy as patient and boring. Waluigi was WRONG, and being wrong about a Corvinarus is a potentially fatal error.

Vivian operated under at least three identities:
- **Vivian** — The real identity. Heir claimant.
- **Vivesna** — The thrall disguise. Weeks of intelligence gathering.
- **vinvessa** — The attack identity. Crimson death beams and axe murders.

The transition from passive to active suggests either a timeline change, a cover breach, or the completion of a planning phase. Vivian's weeks as Vivesna weren't waiting—they were PREPARATION. The corridor fight was Phase Two of a plan that began with Phase One: learning everything about the estate from the inside.

This is the most dangerous kind of enemy: one who already knows your terrain better than you do.

Darius and the Planar Sanctum

The ultimate secret of House Corvinarus lies in the Planar Sanctum—a hidden dimension constructed by Darius. Accessing it requires repairing fractured teleportation circles in the master bedrooms of the various manors.

Repairing these circles requires morbid alchemical components: Bone, freshly cut live wood, incense, iron dust, and chalk powder. The Mages' Guild and the Iron Legion are both seeking access.

'OC' (Orantha Cornelius, the Oracle) and 'AC' left their initials carved into the bedframes of this cursed place. The family's fingerprints are EVERYWHERE.

Waluigi's Assessment

Waluigi does not want to be involved in the Corvinarus succession. Waluigi does not want to be involved with ANY Corvinarus. Waluigi wants to go home, take a long bath, and play tennis on a court that exists in only ONE dimension and ONE time period.

But the reality is that House Corvinarus is the lock, the key, and the door to the current crisis. To fix the Planar Fracture, someone is going to have to breach Darius's Sanctum, deal with the Grafting's fallout, prevent the Three Threads from snapping, AND somehow stop Vivian from killing everyone in the Shadow Estate with magic that ignores the rules.

The situation has gone from 'complicated political inheritance' to 'active hunting ground with reality-ending consequences.' The Corvinarus family doesn't just have skeletons in their closet. Their skeletons are ARMED, MAGICAL, and HUNTING PARTY MEMBERS THROUGH CORRIDORS.

Waluigi will leave the blood magic and ritual chalk to the Mages' Guild. But when it comes time to smash artifacts and claim loot? Waluigi will be there.

Assuming reality holds together long enough. WAH.

name: The Monster Underground
title: The Kingdom Below the Barrier
type: Hidden Subterranean Monarchy / Civilian Realm / Defensive Magic Polity
region: Mount Ebott — Ruins, Snowdin, Hotland, CORE, and the Royal barrier approaches
status: Active; politically insulated; newly exposed to an unauthorized surface survey presence
leader: Royal Family — Toriel and Asgore named as barrier authorities; present command arrangement requires confirmation
headquarters: Royal seat beyond Snowdin; exact administrative location unverified
motto: Unrecorded — the barrier, rather than a slogan, appears to be the state’s defining policy
affiliation: The Monster Underground realm; not a subordinate of the Iron Legion or Regal Empire
summary: The Monster Underground is the living political community beneath Mount Ebott, not simply a hazardous ruin system. Its monarchy controls or can authorize access through the ancient barrier, its towns maintain local social order, and its citizens carry the consequences of a surface history that may have been erased. Waluigi treats the Iron Legion survey as a foreign-contact incident, not a dungeon crawl. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is adding this faction record because too many connected files called the Underground a place when the evidence says it is a polity. A barrier that decides who may leave is border policy. A royal family whose permission is required to cross it is a government. Snowdin’s social response to danger, Sans’s sentry role, the Ruins’ transit paths, and the abandoned police station all show institutions and habits that cannot be reduced to “monsters in caves.” The fact that their paperwork is incomplete does not make them unorganized; it may only mean outsiders have not earned access to the parts that organize them.

Part III makes the Underground’s political problem visible. Sans remembers enough to identify the barrier, the royal exit routes, and Flowey’s royal origin, yet appears unable to hold a stable account of the war that made these systems necessary. Toriel and Asgore are named as authorities but are absent from the field scene. In their absence, a sentry guides strangers, a town rewards whoever visibly stops a threat, and Koffin-K can briefly mistake applause for a mandate. Waluigi reads this not as proof that the monarchy is fake, but as evidence that official authority is distant, compartmentalized, or deliberately quiet at the frontier.

The Iron Legion creates the immediate external risk. Gamma Division’s survey equipment, its manual, its censored dates, and the Agent’s status all arrive before a negotiated contact framework. Mihawk then names an improvised party “the Iron Legion,” importing an imperial identity into Snowdin without authority from either side. This is precisely the kind of ambiguity that turns reconnaissance into occupation in every history Waluigi has ever had the misfortune to read. The Underground’s reaction remains unresolved, but it has every reason to distinguish the people who arrived from the surface from the story those people tell about why they are there.

Flowey is the internal risk that does not fit cleanly into any faction box. He is connected by Sans’s account to the royal family, behaves as a hostile independent actor, and demonstrates the ability to affect Legion technology. Koffin-K is another boundary case: a local theatrical villain with real followers and no demonstrated mandate. Waluigi refuses to pretend either is representative of the entire Underground. He does insist that both reveal stress points — unresolved history, informal authority, and the way an isolated society reacts when outsiders bring machines, titles, and an appetite for classification.

Waluigi’s ruling: treat the Monster Underground as a sovereign political community with unknown internal factions, not as unclaimed terrain. Do not infer consent from hospitality, do not infer weakness from whimsy, and do not let a broken survey machine define the people it was sent to measure. WAH.

name: The Council of Seven
title: Seven Seats, One Vacant, Eight Votes Counted
type: Governing Body / Liberated Toads Cohort Council
status: Sitting — quorum four of seven; the seventh seat vacant since the Mole's exposure
summary: The Council of Seven is the Liberated Toads' Cohort Council: seven elected representatives, one per major cohort, empowered to advise the Speaker and to override a Speaker's veto with a two-thirds majority. Six seats are filled. The seventh — the Scouts' seat — has been vacant since its holder was exposed as the Mole. The name 'Council of Seven' is the one the movement uses when speaking to outsiders, and it is the name that reached the Iron Legion through an interrogation the Legion thought it was winning.
description:
There are two names in the archive for the same body, and the difference between them is a security decision.

Internally, the Liberated Toads call it the Cohort Council. Seven elected representatives, one drawn from each major cohort, sitting to advise the Speaker. The Speaker holds emergency powers and can bypass a council vote in a crisis; the Council can override a veto with a two-thirds majority. Quorum is four. The seats, as recorded:

1. Elder Mudcap
2. Captain Fernback
3. Scribe Dewdrop
4. Forgemaster Ironspore
5. Warden Thornshell
6. Healer Mistpetal
7. VACANT — the Scouts' seat

The seventh seat is not vacant by accident or attrition. It is vacant because the toad who held it was the Mole, and the Scouts cohort remains flagged as compromised. A governing body that has left an empty chair in the room rather than fill it quickly is telling you something about how badly the betrayal went.

## The name the enemy learned

'Council of Seven' enters the Iron Legion's records through the interrogation of the green-dyed decoy who was taken in place of Speaker L. Under questioning the decoy spoke of the Fractured Heart philosophy, of the Council of Seven, and of how the movement would survive any single death. The Legion's own after-action note records that the interrogators got nothing useful and that the decoy performed perfectly — revealing nothing while appearing to break.

Waluigi wishes to be clear about what happened there, because it is easy to miss. The decoy gave the Legion a real name for a real body and it cost the movement nothing, because knowing that seven toads meet is not the same as knowing which seven, or where, or when, or that one of the chairs is empty. The decoy spent an afternoon of Legion attention on a structural fact and kept every operational one. Then Ironhand looked at the reports, worked out he had been sold a performance, and issued Order 120.

## The division list

The archive holds a division list from a sitting of the Council on the question that the resettlement petition be received. It records four to three with one abstention — and seven members producing eight counted votes. The fifth seat's abstention was entered twice and never struck. The seventh seat's aye was cast before the seat was vacated during the sitting.

Waluigi has read a great many instruments in this archive and observes that a division list is normally the one record of a hearing that cannot be redrafted afterwards. This one arrives already wrong, in two directions at once, on the day the seventh seat emptied. Draw from that what you like. Waluigi has drawn several things and intends to keep them to himself until the Accountability Docket catches up. WAH.

name: The Midlands Diet
title: Thirty-Nine Seats, Twenty-Eight of Them Already Spoken For
status: Sitting. Assessed by Iron Legion intelligence as under 'near-total political control'.
summary: The Midlands Diet is the legislative body of the Regal Empire — a 39-seat chamber that passed both the Supernatural Sovereignty Act and the Iron Mandate within three days of each other during the Toad Liberation Crisis. The Iron Legion's own asset register lists 'Midlands Diet Control — 28 of 39 seats aligned' under the heading political, with the note 'near-total political control'. Speaker Rivers sat in this chamber and resigned from it at 09:00 on the 21st of Highsun in protest at the Mandate.
description:
Waluigi files the Midlands Diet under institutions that did their job exactly as designed, which is the worst thing that can be said about a parliament.

## The arithmetic

Thirty-nine seats. The Iron Legion's internal asset register — the same document that counts its infantry and its warlord alliances — has an entry under *political* reading: **Midlands Diet Control, 28 of 39 seats aligned, near-total political control.**

That is not an accusation from an enemy. That is the Legion's own bookkeeping, filed alongside its troop counts, because from the Legion's point of view the Diet is an asset in the same category as a garrison.

Twenty-eight of thirty-nine is 71.8 per cent. Waluigi invites the reader to compare that figure with the recorded division on the Iron Mandate: **28 for, 8 against, 3 abstaining.** Twenty-eight. The Mandate did not persuade a single seat that was not already aligned. The vote was not a debate; it was a headcount that had been taken in advance, and the Legion knew the result before the question was put because the Legion had written down the number weeks earlier.

## What it passed

**18th Highsun, 13:00 — the Supernatural Sovereignty Act.** Organized vampires and werewolves declared illegal; in its posted text, any undertaking to a power outside the mortal establishment made triable as sedition, complete on the giving, with everyone present who did not dissent aloud held to have given it.

**21st Highsun, 09:00 — the Iron Mandate.** Emergency powers to the Iron Legion to purge supernatural threats, and the reclassification of the Liberated Toads as an 'organized supernatural entity'. Passed 28-8-3. Legion patrols mobilised immediately — which tells you the mobilisation orders were cut before the vote.

Three days between them. The first defined the crime; the second decided who was guilty of it. Waluigi does not believe the sequencing was accidental.

## The eleven

The more interesting number is the other one. Eight against, three abstaining. Eleven seats out of thirty-nine were not the Legion's, and the register's phrase 'near-total' is doing quiet work — the Legion counted its own control and privately conceded it was not complete.

One of those seats belonged to **Speaker Rivers**, who resigned at 09:00 on the 21st, the hour the Mandate passed, and then allowed himself to be taken so that a digital virus could be carried inside Aegis Command. Rivers is the only member of this chamber who resigned it and then used the resignation as an operation. Whether the other ten did anything at all is not recorded, which is its own kind of record.

## Standing

The Iron Mandate was later condemned by the Glazed Congress as Vote #200. That condemnation is external. Nothing in the sources shows the Midlands Diet repealing, reviewing, or revisiting either statute. The chamber that passed them has not, on any evidence available to this archive, said a further word about them. WAH.

summary: The DGK is an organized operations group that maintains agents, trackers, an emergency line, sample-containment protocols, and a Central Command. Its authority is compromised by an apparent unauthorized mission and Director Vale's attempt to seize command.
description:
The Dread Mansion transcript provides the first direct field evidence of the DGK's operating structure: agents receive assignments, trackers record last pings, Central Command operates an emergency line, and Spirit Residue is supposed to remain in Level 4 containment. The group can identify a missing operative and ask whether samples are secure.

The same call exposes a command conflict. Central Command denies assigning Liam's retrieval mission and orders the sample put down. Director Vale arrives, presents a badge marked Directorate Global Operations, confiscates Liam's phone, and declares the operation authorized after the fact. Central Command rejects that claim.

The DGK's full name, membership, jurisdiction, and relationship to the Mushroom Kingdom remain unverified beyond the call transcript.

name: The Order of Jack
title: The Jackson Order — A Personal Retinue With a Recruiting Poster's Arithmetic
type: Knightly Order / Household Retinue / Provincial Militia Umbrella
region: Regal Empire — Midlands periphery, seated at Vellanet Rise
status: Active — small standing strength, large paper strength, excellent local reputation
leader: Commander Jack (Jackson) Melvus Miser
headquarters: Vellanet Rise (fortified manor and muster yard)
motto: "Between the road and the harm."
affiliation: Independent order, sworn personally to Jack Miser; backed by the Regal Lion and, at one remove, the Iron Legion
summary: Jack Miser's own body of arms, founded once he had the resources to stop borrowing other people's. Knights, paladins, clerics, fighters, soldiers and levy militias under one white-blue-and-yellow device: a shield fronting crossed swords and a vertical holy staff, winged either side, crowned above. Its quoted strength of 20,000 is a muster roll — levies, unpaid sworn volunteers, hired-out foreign clients, and Regal Lion / Iron Legion personnel already counted elsewhere. The bodies Jack pays and can move tomorrow number in the hundreds. It guards roads, escorts convoys, answers monster calls the Guild will not price, and hires out to neighbouring lords with Jack's permission. Its oath names Jack before it names any crown.
description:
## What It Is

A **personal order**. Not a chapter of a larger institution, not a crown formation — a body of armed men and women who took an oath to a man who then bought them boots.

Jack founded it after eleven years inside the Regal Lion taught him precisely what he wanted and precisely what he could not get by staying: an order that would still exist, and still serve his family, after he was dead.

## The Device

A shield, fronting a cross of swords with a holy staff standing vertical through the join. Wings sprout left and right of the shield. A crown sits above it. White, blue and yellow.

Waluigi has audited a great many heraldic devices and offers one observation: the crown is **above** the shield, not on a head. Read charitably, that is service to the Empire. Read the other way, it is a vacancy notice.

## The Number

The order says **20,000 personnel combined**. That figure appears on its own recruitment sheets, in three ballads, and in at least one Mushroom-side threat estimate that took it at face value.

The roll includes, in one undifferentiated column:

- the paid standing garrison and mounted knights (the real, movable order);
- clerics and paladins on retainer rather than salary;
- **levy militias** from Vellanet Rise's villages, who cannot all be fielded without abandoning a harvest;
- sworn volunteers who wear the badge and have never drawn a wage;
- contracted personnel hired out to foreign lords and clients;
- **Regal Lion and Iron Legion troops counted as "backing"** — men already tallied on Legion rolls, counted twice.

Waluigi's working figure for what Jack can actually pay, house and march tomorrow: a fortified manor's garrison and a few hundred riders. The rest is a mobilization ceiling and a favour network. That is not fraud; it is how every small order's paperwork looks. It is only dangerous because outsiders read it as an order of battle.

## What It Actually Does

Road watch. Convoy escort. Disaster response inside the grant. Monster contracts for towns that cannot afford a Mages' Guild callout. Hired service to neighbouring lords and foreign clients — permitted by Jack explicitly, so that his people can sell capabilities that higher powers demand without going through their own rulers' chains of command.

A meaningful share of its personnel did not join for the Empire, the crown, or the wage. They joined **for Jack**, having grown up on the Myrmidon story. Waluigi files that under *recruitment success* and, in the same breath, under *single point of failure*.

## The Chaplaincy, and the Instruction Nobody Wrote Down

The Order's chaplains are **Silver Flame**, ordained at Flamekeep, because the Regal Lion's are and the Order inherited the Lion's chaplaincy along with its drill and its paperwork. On the establishment table they are unremarkable: a chaplain per standing company, the daily liturgy, the Litany of Purification before a contract, blessings on ammunition on Terras.

Off the establishment table they carry one standing instruction that appears in no order book, no oath text, and no muster return: **the Edict of Purification is not to be raised against a tenant of Vellanet Rise.**

Waluigi has confirmed this from three serving chaplains independently. None would write it down. All three described it in nearly identical words, which in Waluigi's experience means it was said once, clearly, by someone who meant it, and has been repeated ever since.

Consider what that actually is. A commander with no ecclesiastical standing has instructed ordained clergy to disregard a standing edict of their own church, inside territory that church's inquisitors have a formal right of entry to, and the instruction has been obeyed for four years by everyone who received it. That is not a heresy. It is not currently anything, because nobody has filed it. It is, however, a demonstration that the Order's chaplains take their orders from Jack and not from Flamekeep, and a demonstration is exactly the sort of thing an inquisitor is trained to notice.

The oath problem and the chaplaincy problem are the same problem wearing different vestments. The Order's loyalty clause names a man rather than a throne. Its clergy answer a man rather than a church. Neither has been tested. Both will be, by whichever institution gets there first.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Well-run, well-liked, and structurally identical to the first chapter of every provincial warlord's biography ever filed in this archive. The difference so far is entirely the character of one man, which is a lovely thing to say about a person and a terrible thing to say about an institution.

Watch the oath wording. Watch the second holding, if a second holding ever arrives. And watch Flamekeep, which has not yet asked the Order who its chaplains actually work for. WAH.

faiths.note: The Order's chaplains are Flamekeep-ordained because the Regal Lion's are. The Order's standing instruction to those chaplains — do not raise the Edict of Purification against a tenant of the Rise — is not, and has never been, in writing.

title: Iron Legion Special Forces - Four Operatives, Four Colours, One Retrieval
region: Regal Empire - deployed across planar boundaries; currently inside the Overgrown Manor (Feywild)
status: Active - four operatives deployed to the Overgrown Manor on a single-contractor retrieval
leader: Not disclosed to the party; Black did the talking that mattered
headquarters: Unknown - the unit gave the Iron Legion as its parent and the Aegis Magi as its client
motto: Not offered. They introduce themselves by colour and consider that sufficient.
affiliation: Iron Legion; contracted through the Aegis Magi of the Mages' Guild
summary: A four-operative special forces unit - Red, Green, Yellow and Black - sent into the Feywild to retrieve one overdue dwarf. They introduce themselves in sequence with a flourish each, the fourth by turning into a shadow. They apprehended Toad Lee and Waluigi as leverage inside ten minutes of meeting them, which is faster than anything else in this manor has managed.
description:
The Colour Division walked into the middle of a plant war and did not care about the plant war, and the archive wants that on the record first, because it is the whole character of the unit.

They were found behind a locked door on the manor's lower floor, in a room where the household had heard fighting. Three stood, one introduced himself and stopped being a person shape. Their colours are their names, their names are their ranks as far as anybody outside can tell, and when asked who they serve the answer was *special forces* and then, when pressed, *the Iron Legion*.

The deployment order is small and specific: find a dwarf named Hjumpik - rendered, at the point of asking, as *Hjumpoo* - because his time is up. Five nights was the contract. It ran long. The Aegis Magi want their contractor back for the mission, and rather than send a letter they sent four operatives across a planar boundary into a house being eaten by trees.

Their method, observed once and sufficient to characterise them: apprehend the associates, offer the principal a window, and call the associates *insurance*. They arrived with mage cages and put them away when Hjumpik objected; they produced handcuffs instead; they granted an investigation window and started a clock on it. Nothing they did was cruel and nothing they did was negotiable.

Waluigi notes, with an archivist's professional hatred, that the Division is the first organisation in this arc to state its objective plainly, meet its objective efficiently, and leave the party with fewer options than it found them with.

The report gives no scale, leader, headquarters, formal roster, or independently verified organizational details. Waluigi files the name and keeps the blanks.
description:
## What the 2 Aethel report says

During a conversation after a hypno-helmet drone attack, an older woman and a fox-eared Toad invoke the Emerald Enclave. They say the group has stopped letting new people in and describe their effort to prevent Fawful’s forces from completing a dragon-linked ritual. The record does not establish whether both speakers hold formal roles, whether the group has an organized chain of command, or whether its boundaries extend beyond this account.

## What the archive does not know

No member list, leader, headquarters, scale, territory, charter, or independent source is in the record. The fox-eared Toad resembles roster entry #73, Toad ie Foxx, but the account also uses “Konathin” and an unclear “Toad ie Fox” phrase; no roster match is confirmed. The older woman remains unnamed. The Enclave is not assigned formal allies or enemies on the strength of one encounter.

This page files a reported name so future evidence has a place to land. It does not fill in a faction around it.
